what: This Act provides a comprehensive framework for criminal law in India, outlining various offenses and their corresponding punishments. It covers topics such as rioting, giving false information on oath, dowry death, harassment of women, and intentionally damaging or making a ship unsafe.

1.title: Title and ex tent of operation of the Code
1.what: The Indian Penal Code shall be called the Indian Penal Code and applies to the entire country of India.

2.title: Punishment of of fences committed within India
2.what: Any person who commits an offense within India can be punished only under this Indian Penal Code

3.title: Punishment of offences committed beyond, but which by law may be tried within, India
3.what: A person who must comply with Indian law and is tried for a crime that was actually committed outside India, will be treated as if the crime was committed inside India.

4.title: Extension of Code to extra-territorial offences
4.what: The provisions of this Code apply also to any offence committed by— (1) any citizen of India in any place without and beyond India; (2) any person on any ship or aircraft registered in India wherever it may be.

5.title: Certain laws not to be affected by this Act
5.what: Nothing in this Act affects laws punishing mutiny and desertion from government service, or special/local laws regarding these matters.

6.title: Definitions in the Code to be und erstood subject to exceptions
6.what: Definitions in the Code shall be understood subject to exceptions contained in the Chapter entitled 'General Exceptions', unless those exceptions are mentioned in the definition or illustration.

7.title: Sense of expression once explained
7.what: Every time a word or phrase is defined in one place in the Indian Penal Code 1860, it must be used exactly as explained throughout the entire code.

9.title: Number
9.what: Words in the singular form are also accepted as in the plural form and vice versa.

11.title: “Person”
11.what: The term 'person' includes any company or association, whether it is a corporation or not.

12.title: “Public”
12.what: The term 'public' means any group of people, regardless of their social status.

19.title: “Judge”
19.what: A person who officially gives judgments in legal proceedings, or is part of a group that does so, is considered a 'judge'. This includes those with specific powers given by law.

20.title: “Court of Justice”
20.what: A Court of Justice is a judge or body of judges empowered by law to act judicially alone or together.

21.title: “Public servant ”
21.what: A public servant is any person falling under one of the following descriptions:

23.title: “Wrongful gain”
23.what: Wrongful gain and loss occur when a person gains or loses property illegally, even if they were not originally entitled to it.

24.title: “Dishonestly”
24.what: A person intentionally acts in a way that causes someone else to gain something they shouldn't have or loses something they should have. This act is considered 'dishonest'

25.title: “Fraudulently”
25.what: A person is said to do a thing fraudulently if they intend to deceive but not necessarily succeed.

26.title: “Reason to believe ”
26.what: A person has 'reason to believe' something if they have enough reason to think it's true, but not necessarily enough to prove it.

27.title: “Property in possession of wife, clerk or servant”
27.what: Property in possession of wife, clerk or servant

28.title: “Counterfeit”
28.what: Counterfeiting - Causing one thing to resemble another with intention to deceive.

29.title: “Document”
29.what: Any matter expressed or described on a substance using letters, figures, or marks, intended to be used as evidence.

29A.title: “Electronic record”
29A.what: The term "electronic record" means what is defined in clause (t) of sub-section (1) of section 2 of the Information Technology Act, 2000.

30.title: “Valuable security”
30.what: A document that creates, extends, transfers, restricts, extinguishes, or releases a legal right, or acknowledges liability for a certain right.

32.title: Words referring to acts inclu de illegal omissions
32.what: Words referring to acts include illegal omissions

34.title: Acts done by several persons in fu rtherance of common intention
34.what: When multiple people perform an action together to further the shared goal of the group, each individual can be held responsible for the entire action as if they did it alone.

35.title: When such an act is criminal by reason of its being done with a cr iminal knowledge or
35.what: When an act that is criminal due to being done with criminal knowledge or intention is carried out by multiple people, each person who participated with that knowledge or intention is held responsible for the entire act as if they had done it alone with that knowledge or intention.

36.title: Effect caused partly by act and partly by omission
36.what: If doing something or not doing something together causes a result, it's the same crime whether you did one part of it with an act (like hitting someone) and another part with neglecting to do something (like not giving food).

37.title: Co -operation by doing one of several acts constituting an offence
37.what: When someone intentionally helps commit a crime by doing one part of the crime, they can be held guilty even if their action was just one part of the whole crime.

38.title: Persons concerned in criminal act may be guilty of different offences
38.what: Where several persons are engaged or concerned in the commission of a criminal act, they may be guilty of different offences by means of that act.

39.title: “Voluntarily”
39.what: A person is said to cause an effect “voluntarily” when he causes it by means whereby he intended to cause it, or by means which, at the time of employing those means, he knew or had reason to believe to be likely to cause it.

40.title: “Offence”
40.what: Except in the 2[Chapters] and sections mentioned in clauses 2 and 3 of this section, the word “offence” denotes a thing made punishable by this Code.

41.title: “Special law”
41.what: A “special law” is a law applicable to a particular subject.

42.title: “Local law”
42.what: A “local law” is a law applicable only to a particular part of India.

43.title: “Illegal”. “Legally bound to do ”
43.what: The word “illegal” is applicable to everything which is an offence or which is prohibited by law, or which furnishes ground for a civil action; and a person is said to be “legally bound to do” whatever it is illegal in him to omit.

44.title: “Injury”
44.what: The word “injury” denotes any harm whatever illegally caused to any person, in body, mind, reputation or property.

45.title: “Life”
45.what: The word “life” denotes the life of a human being, unless the con trary appears from the context.

46.title: “Death”
46.what: The word “death” denotes the death of a human being unless the contrary appears from the context.

47.title: “Animal”
47.what: The word “animal” denotes any living creature, other than a human being.

52.title: “Good faith”
52.what: Nothing is said to be done or believed in good faith which is done or believed without due care and attention.

53.title: Punishments
53.what: Offenders are liable to death, imprisonment for life, rigorous imprisonment, simple imprisonment, forfeiture of property, or fine.

53A.title: Construction o f reference to transportation
53A.what: Any reference to “transportation for life” in other laws is now referred to as “imprisonment for life”. References to shorter terms of transportation are considered omitted.

54.title: Commutation of sentence of death
54.what: In every case in which sentence of death shall have been passed, the appropriate Government may, without the consent of the offender, commute the punishment for any other punishment provided by this Code.

55.title: Commutation of sent ence of imprisonment for life
55.what: The appropriate Government can commute the punishment for imprisonment for life to a term not exceeding fourteen years.

57.title: Fra ctions of terms of punishment
57.what: Fractions of terms of punishment: Imprisonment for life is equivalent to imprisonment for twenty years.

60.title: Sentence may be (in certain cases of imprisonment) wholly or partly rigorous or simple
60.what: The court can decide if the sentence should be wholly rigorous, wholly simple, or a mix of both.

63.title: Amount of fine
63.what: The fine for an offense can be any amount, but it cannot be too high.

64.title: Sentence of impriso nment for non-payment of fine
64.what: If someone is fined and doesn't pay, they can get extra time in prison on top of their original sentence.

65.title: Limit to imprisonment for non -payment of fine, when imprisonment and fine awardable
65.what: The term for which the Court directs the offender to be imprisoned in default of payment of a fine shall not exceed one-fourth of the term of imprisonment which is the maximum fixed for the offence, if the offence be punishable with imprisonment as well as fine.

66.title: Description of impriso nment for non -payment of fine
66.what: The imprisonment imposed by the Court may be of any description that was originally intended for the offence.

67.title: Imprisonment for non-payment of fine, when offence punishable with fine only
67.what: If an offence is punishable with a fine only, the court can impose a simple imprisonment (not exceeding 2 months if the fine is ≤ ₹50, 4 months if the fine is ≤ ₹100, and 6 months otherwise) and direct the offender to be imprisoned for a term not exceeding these limits.

68.title: Imprisonment to terminate on payment of fine
68.what: Imprisonment will end when a fine is paid or legally enforced.

69.title: Termination of imprisonment on payment of proportional part of fine
69.what: If you pay a proportionate part of your fine before your prison term ends, and the amount you pay is less than what you still owe, you will be released from prison when your original sentence period ends.

70.title: Fine leviable within six years, of during imprisonment. Death not to discharge property from
70.what: The fine or unpaid part of it can be levied within 6 years of passing the sentence. If imprisonment is more than 6 years, it can be levied before that period ends. Death does not release liability for property after death.

71.title: Limit of punishment of offence made up of several offences
71.what: If an offense is made up of parts, where each part is also an offense, the offender should not be punished with more than one punishment unless specified otherwise. If multiple laws define the same offense or if combining acts results in a different offense, the offender should not receive a harsher punishment than what could have been given for any individual offense.

72.title: Punishment of person guilty of one of several offences, the judgment stating that it is doubtful
72.what: If a person is found guilty of one of several offences listed in the judgment, but it's unclear which one they're guilty of, punish them with the lowest punishment listed if it applies to all.

73.title: Solitary confinement
73.what: Whenever any person is convicted of an offence for which under this Code the Court has power to sentence him to rigorous imprisonment, the Court may, by its sentence, order that the offender shall be kept in solitary confinement for any portion or portions of the imprisonment to which he is sentenced, not exceeding three months in the whole, according to the following scale, that is to say— a time not exceeding one month if the term of imprisonment shall not exceed six months; a time not exceeding two months if the term of imprisonment shall exceed six months and 1[shall not exceed one] year a time not exceeding three months if the term of imprisonment shall exceed one year.

74.title: Limit of solitary confinement
74.what: In executing a sentence of solitary confinement, the maximum time that can be spent in solitary confinement at a time is 14 days. After this, there must be an interval of at least the same length. If the total imprisonment exceeds 3 months, then the maximum solitary confinement time per month cannot exceed 7 days, with the same intervals.

75.title: Enhanced punishment for certain offences under Chapter XII or Chapter X VII after
75.what: If you have been previously convicted of an offence under Chapter XII or XVII with a sentence of three years or more, and then commit another offence under the same chapters, you can face imprisonment for life or up to 10 years.

76.title: Act done by a person bound, or by mistake of fact believing himself bound, by law
76.what: A person who is bound by law or believes themselves to be bound in good faith cannot be guilty of an offense.

77.title: Act of Judg e when actin g judicially
77.what: A judge cannot be guilty of an offense if they are acting judicially and using a power that they believe is given to them by law in good faith.

78.title: Act done pursuant to the judgment or order of Court
78.what: Nothing done in pursuance of a court's judgment or order, while it is still in force, is an offense unless done in bad faith.

79.title: Act done by a person justified, or by mistake of fact believi ng himself, justified, by law
79.what: A person who believes they are justified by law and acts in good faith, even if they make a mistake of fact, is not committing an offense.

80.title: Accident in doing a lawful act
80.what: Nothing is an offence which is done by accident or misfortune, without any criminal intention or knowledge, while doing a lawful act in a lawful manner with proper care and caution.

81.title: Act likely to cause harm, but done without criminal intent, and to prevent other harm
81.what: Nothing is an offence merely by reason of its being done with the knowledge that it is likely to cause harm, if it be done without any criminal intention to cause harm, and in good faith for the purpose of preventing or avoiding other harm to person or property.

82.title: Act of a child under seven years of age
82.what: A child under seven years of age cannot be held criminally responsible for any action.

83.title: Act of a child above seven and under twe lve of immature understanding
83.what: A child between 7 and 12 years old who lacks enough understanding to make informed decisions is not considered guilty for an action they commit.

84.title: Act of a person of unsound mind
84.what: A person who commits an act while being mentally unsound cannot be held guilty if they did not know the nature of the act or that it was wrong/contrary to law.

85.title: Act of a person incapable of judgment by reason of intoxic ation caused against his will
85.what: A person who commits an act while under the influence of something they were forced to take and can't understand what they're doing is not guilty of a crime.

86.title: Offence requiring a particular intent or knowledge committed by one who is intoxicated
86.what: A person who commits an act that requires a particular intent or knowledge while intoxicated shall be treated as having the same intent or knowledge as they would have if they were sober.

87.title: Act not intended and not k nown to be likely to cause death or gri evous hurt, done by
87.what: Nothing that causes harm to someone who has given consent is a crime, unless it's intended to cause death or serious injury.

88.title: Act not intended to cause death, done by consent in good faith for person's benefit
88.what: Nothing is an offense if it causes harm in good faith for someone's benefit, with their consent, even if the person intends to cause death or knows it may cause death.

89.title: Act done in good faith for benefit of child or insane person, by or by consent of guardian
89.what: Nothing which is done in good faith for the benefit of a person under twelve years of age, or of unsound mind, by or by consent, either express or implied, of the guardian or other person having lawful charge of that person, is an offence by reason of any harm which it may cause, or be intended by the doer to cause or be known by the doer to be likely to cause to that person: Provided— Provisos. First.—That this exception shall not extend to the intentional causing of death, or to the attempting to cause death; Secondly.—That this exception shall not extend to the doing of anything which the person doing it knows to be likely to cause death, for any purpose other than the preventing of death or grievous hurt, or the curing of any grievous disease or infirmity; Thirdly.—That this exception shall not extend to the voluntary causing of grievous hurt, or to the attempting to cause grievous hurt, unless it be for the purpose of preventing death or grievous hurt, or the curing of any grievous disease or infirmity; Fourthly.—That this exception shall not extend to the abetment of any offence, to the committing of which offence it would not extend.

90.title: Consent known to be given under fear or misconception
90.what: A consent is not valid if it was given due to fear or misconception, and the person knows or has reason to believe this.

91.title: Exclusion of acts which are offences independently of harm cause
91.what: Acts that are offences independently of harm caused, and exceptions to these acts.

92.title: Act done in good faith for benefit of a person without consent
92.what: Nothing is an offence by reason of any harm which it may cause to a person for whose benefit it is done in good faith, even without that person's consent, if the circumstances are such that it is impossible for that person to signify consent, or if that person is incapable of giving consent, and has no guardian or other person in lawful charge of him from whom it can be obtained in time for the thing to be done with benefit.

93.title: Communication made in good faith
93.what: Communication made in good faith is not an offense if it is made for the benefit of the person to whom it is made.

94.title: Act to which a p erson is compelled by threats
94.what: A person who commits an act that would be illegal if they weren't threatened with death, can be excused from criminal liability if they were forced to do it by threats and there was a reasonable fear of immediate death.

95.title: Act causing slight harm
95.what: Nothing is an offence by reason that it causes, or that it is intended to cause, or that it is known to be likely to cause, any harm, if that harm is so slight that no person of ordinary sense and temper would complain of such harm.

96.title: Things done in private defence
96.what: Nothing is an offence which is done in the exercise of the right of private defence.

97.title: Right of private defence of the body and of property
97.what: A person has the right to defend their own body and property against certain crimes, including theft, robbery, and trespassing.

98.title: Right of private defence against the act of a person of unsound mind, etc
98.what: A person who commits an act due to a mental or physical condition (youth, lack of understanding, insanity, intoxication) is entitled to the same rights of self-defence as they would have if they were sane.

99.title: Acts against which there is no right of private defence
99.what: There is no right of private defence against an act that does not reasonably cause fear of death or serious injury, if done by a public servant acting in good faith under their office, or by direction of a public servant. The right to defend oneself only extends to what is necessary for self-defence.

100.title: When the right of private defence of the body extends to causing death
100.what: The right to self-defense extends to causing death or harm to an attacker if they are committing one of the following types of offenses: threatening death, serious injury, rape, unnatural lust, kidnapping, wrongful confinement, or attempting to throw acid that could cause serious injury.

101.title: When such right extends to causing any harm other than death
101.what: If an offence is not listed in section 100, the right to private defence of one's body extends to voluntarily causing harm to the attacker (not resulting in death), but with restrictions mentioned in section 99.

102.title: Commencement and continuance of the right o f private defence of the body
102.what: The right of private defence of the body commences as soon as a reasonable apprehension of danger to the body arises from an attempt or threat to commit the offence though the offence may not have been committed; and it continues as long as such apprehension of danger to the body continues.

103.title: When the right of private defence of property extends to causing death
103.what: The right of private defence of property extends, under the restrictions mentioned in section 99, to the voluntary causing of death or of any other harm to the wrong-doer, if the offence, the committing of which, or the attempting to commit which, occasions the exercise of the right, be an offence of any of the descriptions enumerated, namely:— First.—Robbery; Secondly.—House-breaking by night; Thirdly.—Mischief by fire committed on any building, tent or vessel, which building, tent or vessel is used as a human dwelling, or as a place for the custody of property; Fourthly.—Theft, mischief, or house-trespass, under such circumstances as may reasonably cause apprehension that death or grievous hurt will be the consequence, if such right of private defence is not exercised.

104.title: When such right extends to causing any harm other than death
104.what: If an offence (like theft, mischief, or trespass) doesn't involve killing someone, you can defend yourself by causing them physical harm, but not fatal harm.

105.title: Commencement and continuance of the right o f private defence of property
105.what: The right of private defence of property commences when a reasonable apprehension of danger to the property occurs, and continues until the offender has retreated with the property or public authorities have assisted in recovering it. The duration of the right varies depending on the type of offence: against theft until the offender retreats or is recovered; against robbery as long as the offender causes harm or death; against criminal trespass/mischief as long as the offender continues the crime; and against house-breaking by night as long as the trespass continues.

106.title: Ri ght of private defence against deadly assault when there is risk of harm to innocent
106.what: If in exercising private defense against an assault that causes reasonable fear of death, a person can't defend without risking harm to an innocent person, their right still extends to running that risk.

107.title: Abetment of a thing
107.what: A person abets the doing of a thing by: 1) Instigating someone to do it, 2) Engaging in a conspiracy with others to do it, or 3) Intentionally aiding the doing of it.

108.title: Abettor
108.what: A person abets an offence, who abets either the commission of an offence, or the commission of an act which would be an offence, if committed by a person capable by law of committing an offence with the same intention or knowledge as that of the abettor.

108A.title: Abetment in India of offences outside India
108A.what: A person abets an offence by instigating someone outside India to commit an act that would be an offence if committed in India.

109.title: Punishment of abetment if the act abetted is committed in consequence and where no express
109.what: The person who abets an offense will be punished with the same punishment as the offense if the act is committed in consequence of the abetment and no express provision is made for its punishment.

110.title: Punishment of abetment if person abetted does act with different intention from that of
110.what: If someone abets an offense but the person they're abetting does it with a different intention, the abettor will be punished as if they had intended to commit the original offense.

111.title: Liability of abettor when one act abetted and different act done
111.what: When an Act is abetted and a different act is done, the abettor is liable for the act done, in the same manner and to the same extent as if he had directly abetted it: Provided the act done was a probable consequence of the abetment, and was committed under the influence of the instigation, or with the aid or in pursuance of the conspiracy which constituted the abetment.

112.title: Abettor when liable to cumulative punishment for act abetted and for act done
112.what: If the act for which the abettor is liable under the last preceding section is committed in addition to the act abetted, and constitute a distinct offence, the abettor is liable to punishment for each of the offences.

113.title: Liability of abettor for an effect caused by the act abetted d ifferent from that intended by
113.what: When an act is abetted with the intention on the part of the abettor of causing a particular effect, and an act for which the abettor is liable in consequence of the abetment, causes a different effect from that intended by the abettor, the abettor is liable for the effect caused, in the same manner and to the same extent as if he had abetted the act with the intention of causing that effect.

114.title: Abettor present when offence is committed
114.what: Whenever any person, who is absent would be liable to be punished as an abettor, is present when the act or offence for which he would be punishable in consequence of the abetment is committed, he shall be deemed to have committed such act or offence.

115.title: Abetment of offence punishable with death or imprisonment for life
115.what: if offence not committed.—Whoever abets the commission of an off ence punishable with death or 1[imprisonment for life], shall, if that offence be not committed in consequence of the abetment, and no express provision is made by this Code for the punishment of such abetment, be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine; if act causin g harm be done in consequence .—and if any act for which the abettor is liable in consequence of the abetment, and which causes hurt to any person, is done, the abettor shall be liable to imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to fourteen years, and shall also be liable to fine.

116.title: Abetment of offence punishable with imprisonment—if offence be not committed
116.what: Whoever abets an offence punishable with imprisonment shall, if that offence be not committed in consequence of the abetment, and no express provision is made by this Code for the punishment of such abetment, be punished with imprisonment of any description provided for that offence for a term which may extend to one-fourth part of the longest term provided for that offence; or with such fine as is provided for that offence, or with both;

117.title: Abetting commission of offence by the public or by more than ten persons
117.what: Whoever abets the commission of an offence by the public generally or by any number or class of persons exceeding ten, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three yea rs, or with fine, or with both.

118.title: Concealing design to commit offence punishable with d eath or imprisonment for life
118.what: A person who tries to hide or lie about a plan to commit a serious crime (like death or life imprisonment) can be punished with up to 7 years in jail and/or a fine. If no such crime happens, they can still get up to 3 years in jail and/or a fine.

119.title: Public servant concealing design to commit offence which it is his duty to prevent
119.what: A public servant who intentionally hides or provides false information about a crime they are supposed to prevent can be punished with imprisonment or fine.

120.title: Concealing design to commit offence punishable with imprisonment
120.what: Concealing design to commit an offence punishable with imprisonment: Voluntarily concealing existence of a design to commit an offence or making false representation about it.

120A.title: Definition of criminal conspiracy
120A.what: Two or more persons agree to do an illegal act or an act not illegal by illegal means. An agreement to commit an offence requires action taken in pursuance of it to be a criminal conspiracy.

120B.title: Punishment of criminal c onspiracy
120B.what: A person who is part of a criminal plan to commit an offense that can result in death or life imprisonment will be punished as if they had directly committed the offense. A person who is part of any other type of conspiracy will face up to 6 months in prison, or a fine, or both.

121.title: Waging, or attempting to wage war, or abetting waging of war, ag ainst the Government of
121.what: Waging, or attempting to wage war, or abetting waging of war, ag ainst the Government of India.—Whoever wages war against the 2[Government of India], or attempts to wage such war, or abets the waging of such war, shall be punished with death, or 1[imprisonment for life]

121A.title: Conspiracy to commit offences punishable by section 121
121A.what: Conspires to commit an offence punishable by section 121, or overawes the Central Government or State Government using criminal force, and can be punished with imprisonment for life or up to 10 years and a fine.

122.title: Collecting arms, etc., with intention of waging war ag ainst th e Government of India
122.what: Collecting arms, etc., with intention of waging war against the Government of India

123.title: Concealing with intent to facilitate design to wage war
123.what: A person who intentionally hides information about a plan to attack the government of India, or fails to report it, can face up to 10 years in prison and a fine.

124.title: Assaulting President, Governor, etc., with intent to compel or restrain the exercise of any
124.what: A person who assaults the President of India, Governor of a state, or attempts to do so, can face up to 7 years in prison and a fine.

124A.title: Sedition
124A.what: Whoever by words, either spoken or written, or by signs, or by visible representation, or otherwise, brings or attempts to bring into hatred or contempt, or excites or attempts t o excite disaffection towards the Government established in India, shall be punished with imprisonment for life, to which fine may be added, or with imprisonment which may extend to three years, to which fine may be added, or with fine.

125.title: Waging war against any Asiatic Power in alliance with the Government of India
125.what: Whoever wages war against the Government of any Asiatic Power in alliance or at peace with the Government of India or attempts to wage such war, or abets the waging of such war, shall be punished with imprisonment for life, to which fine may be added, or with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, to which fine may be added, or with fine.

126.title: Committing depredation on territories of Power at peace with the Government of India
126.what: Whoever commits depredation on the territories of a Power at peace with the Government of India shall be punished with imprisonment for up to 7 years and may also face fine and forfeiture of property used in committing the act.

127.title: Receiving prope rty taken by war or depredation men tioned in sections 125 and 126
127.what: Receiving stolen property from war or depredation; punishment - imprisonment up to 7 years, fine, and forfeiture of property.

128.title: Public servant voluntarily allowing priso ner of state or war to escape
128.what: A public servant who has custody of a state prisoner or prisoner of war and allows them to escape will face up to 10 years in prison and/or a fine.

129.title: Public servant negligently suffering such prisoner to escape
129.what: Whoever, being a public servant and having the custody of any State prisoner or prisoner of war, negligently suffers such prisoner to escape from any place of confinement in which such prisoner is confined, shall be punished with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years, and shall also be liable to fine.

130.title: Aiding escape of, rescuing or harbouring such prisoner
130.what: A person who knowingly helps a prisoner escape or rescues them will face imprisonment for life or up to 10 years and a fine.

131.title: Abetting mutiny, or attempting to seduce a soldier, s ailor or airman from his duty
131.what: A person who helps someone else commit mutiny in the army, navy, or air force, or tries to persuade someone to leave their job, can get up to 10 years in prison and/or a fine.

132.title: Abetment of mutiny, if mutiny is com mitted in consequence thereof
132.what: A person who encourages someone else to lead a mutiny in the army will face punishment, including death, life imprisonment, or up to 10 years in prison, and may also have to pay a fine.

133.title: Abetment of assault by soldier, sailor or airman on his superior officer, when in execution
133.what: Abetting an assault by a soldier, sailor or airman on their superior officer while performing official duties will result in up to 3 years of imprisonment and a fine.

134.title: Abetment of such assault, if the assault committed
134.what: Abetting an assault by a military personnel on a superior officer while performing official duties, punishable by up to 7 years imprisonment and fine.

135.title: Abetment of desertion of soldier, sailor or airman
135.what: A person who helps someone else desert from their job in the army, navy, or air force will get up to 2 years in prison, or a fine, or both.

136.title: Harbouring deserter
136.what: Harbouring deserter: Knowingly harbours an officer, soldier, sailor, or airman who has deserted, and may face imprisonment for up to 2 years or fine.

137.title: Deserter concealed on board merchant vessel through negligence of master
137.what: The master or person in charge of a merchant vessel, on board of which any deserter from the Army, Navy or Air Force of the Government of India is concealed, shall, though ignorant of such concealment, be liable to a penalty not exceeding five hundred rupees, if he might have known of such concealment but for some neglect of his duty as such master or person in charge, or but for some want of discipline on board of the vessel.

138.title: Abetment of act of insubordinatio n by soldier, sailor or airman
138.what: Abetment of act of insubordination by an officer, soldier, sailor or airman in the Army, Navy or Air Force of the Government of India.

139.title: Persons subject to certain Acts
139.what: No person serving in the army, navy, or air force can be punished under this law if they are also subject to another specific act.

140.title: Wearing garb or carrying token used by soldier, sailor or airman
140.what: Wearing garb or carrying token used by soldier, sailor or airman in the Military, Naval or Air service of the Government of India with intention to deceive others that he is such a soldier, sailor or airman.

141.title: Unlawful assembly
141.what: An assembly of five or more persons is considered

142.title: Bein g member of unlawful assembly
142.what: A person who knowingly joins or stays in an illegal group will be considered a part of that illegal group.

143.title: Punishment
143.what: A person who is part of an illegal group can get up to 6 months in jail, or a fine, or both.

144.title: Joining unlawful assem bly armed with deadly weapon
144.what: A person who is part of an unlawful assembly and is armed with a deadly weapon will be punished with imprisonment, fine, or both, for up to two years.

145.title: Joining or continuing in unlawful assembly, knowing it has been commanded to disperse
145.what: Whoever joins or continues in an unlawful assembly, knowing it has been commanded to disperse, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extent to two years, or with fine, or with both.

146.title: Rioting
146.what: Whenever force or violence is used by an unlawful assembly, or by any member thereof, in prosecution of the common object of such assembly, every member of such assembly is guilty of the offence of rioting.

147.title: Punishment for rioting
147.what: Whoever is guilty of rioting, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.

148.title: Rioting, armed with deadly weapon
148.what: Whoever is guilty of rioting, being armed with a deadly weapon or with anything which, used as a weapon of offence, is likely to cause death, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both.

149.title: Every member of unlawful assembly guilty of offence committed in prosecution of common
149.what: If an offence is committed by any member of an unlawful assembly in prosecution of the common object of that assembly, or such as the members of that assembly knew to be likely to be committed in prosecution of that object, every person who, at the time of the committing of that offence, is a member of the same assembly, is guilty of that offence.

150.title: Hiring, or conniving at hiring, of pers ons to join unlawful assembly
150.what: Whoever hires or engages, or employs, or promotes, or connives at hiring, engagement or employment of any person to join or become a member of any unlawful assembly, shall be punishable as a member of such unlawful assembly, and for any offence which may be committed by any such person as a member of such unlawful assembly in pursuance of such hiring, engagement or employment, in the same manner as if he had been a member of such unlawful assembly, or himself had committed such offence.

151.title: Knowingly joining or continuing in assembly of five or more persons after it h as been
151.what: Whoever knowingly joins or continues in any assembly of five or more persons likely to cause a disturbance of the public peace, after such assembly has been lawfully commanded to disperse, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine, or with both.

152.title: Assaulting or obstructing public serva nt when suppressing riot, etc
152.what: Whoever assaults or threatens to assault, or obstructs or attempts to obstruct, any public servant in the discharge of his duty as such public servant, in endeavou ring to disperse an unlawful assembly, or to suppress a riot or affray, or uses, or threatens, or attempts to use criminal force to such public servant, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both.

153.title: Want only giving provoca tion with intent to cause riot
153.what: Whoever malignantly, or wantonly by doing anything which is illegal, gives provocation to any person intending or knowing it to be likely that such provocation will cause the offence of rioting to be committed, shall, if the offence of rioting be committed in consequence of such provocation, be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine, or with both; and if the offence of rioting be not committed, with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine, or with both.

153A.title: Promoting enmity between different groups on ground of re ligion, race, place of birth,
153A.what: Promotes or attempts to promote disharmony between different groups based on religion, race, place of birth, residence, language, caste, or community, or commits acts prejudicial to harmony, causing fear or alarm among members of a group.

153AA.title: Punishment for knowingly carrying arms in any proces sion or organising, or holding
153AA.what: Carrying arms in a public place during a procession or mass drill without permission from a public notice or order issued under section 144A of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, is punishable with up to six months imprisonment and a fine of up to ₹2,000.

153B.title: Imputations, assertions prejudicial to national integration
153B.what: Imputations that can lead to national integration issues, such as making false claims about a person's loyalty to the Constitution or their rights as citizens, can result in up to 3-year imprisonment, fines, or both.

154.title: Owner or occupier of land on which an unlawful assembly is held
154.what: The owner or occupier of land where an unlawful assembly is held must report the incident to the police if they know about it or have reason to believe it will happen, and fail to do so.

155.title: Liability of person for whose benefit riot is committed
155.what: A person who benefits from a riot, including the owner or occupier of land related to it, can be punished with a fine if they knew about the likely occurrence of the riot and failed to prevent it.

156.title: Liability of agent of owner or occupier for whose benefit riot is committed
156.what: Whenever a riot is committed for the benefit or on behalf of any person who is the owner or occupier of any land respecting which such riot takes place, or who claims any interest in such land, or in the subject of any dispute which gave rise to the riot, or who has accepted or derived any benefit therefrom, the agent or manager of such person shall be punishable with fine, if such a gent or manager, having reason to believe that such riot was likely to be committed, or that the unlawful assembly by which such riot was committed was likely to be held, shall not use all lawful means in his power to prevent such riot or assembly from taking place and for suppressing and dispersing the same.

157.title: Harbouring persons h ired for an unlawful assembly
157.what: Harboring persons hired for an unlawful assembly: Whoever harbours, receives or assembles any person knowing they are hired to join an unlawful assembly, shall be punished with imprisonment of up to 6 months, or fine, or both.

158.title: Being hired to take part in an unlawful assembly or riot
158.what: A person who helps take part in an unlawful assembly or riot can face up to 6 months in prison, a fine, or both. If they go armed during this time, they can face up to 2 years in prison, a fine, or both.

159.title: Affray
159.what: Two or more persons who fight in a public place and disturb the public peace are committing an affray.

160.title: Pun ishment for committing affray
160.what: Whoever commits an affray, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one month, or with fine which may extend to one hundred rupees, or with both.

166.title: Public servant disobeying law, with intent to cause injury to any person
166.what: A public servant who knowingly disobeys a law direction intending to cause or knowing it may cause injury to someone will be punished with up to 1 year imprisonment, fine, or both.

166A.title: Public servant disobeying direction under law
166A.what: Whoever, being a public servant,— (a) knowingly disobeys any direction of the law which prohibits him from requiring the attendance at any place of any person for the purpose of investigation into an offence or any other matter, or (b) knowingly disobeys, to the prejudice of any person, any other direction of the law regulating the manner in which he shall conduct such investigation, or (c) fails to record any information given to him under sub-section (1) of section 154 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (2 of 1974), in relation to cognizable offence punishable under section 326A, section 326B, section 354, section 354B, section 370, section 370A, section 376, section 376A, 2[section 376AB, section 376B, section 376C, section 376D, section 376DA, section 376DB] , section 376E or section 509, shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than six months but which may extend to two years, and shall also be liable to fine.

166B.title: Punishment for non-treatment of victim
166B.what: Whoever, being in charge of a hospital, public or private, whether run by the Central Government, the State Government, local bodies or any other person, contravenes the provisions of section 357C of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (2 of 1974), shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year or with fine or with both.

167.title: Public servant framing an incorrect document with intent to cause injury
167.what: Whoever, being a public servant, and being, as such public servant, charged with the preparation or translation of any document or electronic record , frames , prepares or translates that document or electronic record} {

168.title: Public servant unlawfully engaging in trade
168.what: A public servant who is not allowed to engage in trade but does so anyway can get up to 1 year in jail, or a fine, or both.

169.title: Public servant unlawfully buying or bidding for property
169.what: A public servant who is not allowed to buy or bid for certain property purchases it anyway and can face up to 2 years in jail, a fine, or both. The property will be taken away.

170.title: Personating a public servant
170.what: Personating a public servant: Pretending to hold an office as a public servant, knowing you don't, or falsely pretending someone else does, and doing acts under that assumed character.

171.title: Wearing garb or carrying token used by public servant with fraudulent intent
171.what: Wearing garb or carrying token used by public servant with fraudulent intent: If someone not belonging to a certain class of public servants wears or carries something that resembles their uniform, with the intention to deceive others about their identity, they can face imprisonment for up to 3 months, fine up to ₹200, or both.

171A.title: “Candidate”, “Electoral right” defined
171A.what: a person who has been nominated as a candidate at any election

171B.title: Bribery
171B.what: Whoever— (i) gives a gratification to any person with the object of inducing him or any other person to exercise any electoral right or of rewarding any person for having exercised any such right; or (ii) accepts either for himself or for any other person any gratification as a reward for exercising any such right or for inducing or attempting to induce any other person to exercise any such right, commits the offence of bribery: Provided that a declaration of public policy or a promise of public action shall not be an offence under this section.

171C.title: Undue influence at elections
171C.what: Whoever voluntarily interferes or attempts to interfere with the free exercise of any electoral right commits the offence of undue influence at an election.

171D.title: Personation at elections
171D.what: Personation at elections: Whoever applies for a voting paper on someone else's name, or votes once and then applies for a paper in their own name, or abets someone to vote by any means, commits an offence.

171E.title: Punishment for bribery
171E.what: Whoever commits the offence of bribery shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine, or with both: Provided that bribery by treating shall be punished with fine only.

171F.title: Punishment for undue influence or personation at an elect ion
171F.what: A person who uses undue influence or impersonates someone else at an election can be imprisoned for up to 1 year, fined, or both.

171G.title: False statement in connection with an election
171G.what: Making or publishing a false statement about a candidate's personal character or conduct during an election can result in a fine.

171H.title: Illegal payments i n connection with an election
171H.what: A person who spends money without the candidate's permission on promoting their election will get a fine of up to 500 rupees. If they spend less than 10 rupees and get the candidate's written approval within 10 days, it's considered with the candidate's permission.

172.title: Absconding to avoid service of summons or other proceeding
172.what: A person who runs away to avoid receiving a summons, notice, or order from a public servant will be punished with imprisonment for up to one month or a fine of up to ₹500, or both. If the summons is to attend in person or by agent, or to produce a document or electronic record in court, the punishment can be up to six months' imprisonment or a fine of up to ₹1,000, or both.

173.title: Preventing service of summons or other proceeding, or preventing publication thereof
173.what: Preventing service of summons or other proceeding, or preventing publication thereof: Whoever in any manner intentionally prevents the serving on himself, or on any other person, of any summons, notice or order proceeding from any public servant legally competent, as such public servant, to issue such summons, notice or order, or intentionally prevents the lawful affixing to any place of any such summons, notice or order, or intentionally removes any such summons, notice or order from any place to which it is lawfully affixed, or intentionally prevents the lawful making of any proclamation, under the authority of any public servant legally competent, as such public servant, to direct such proclamation to be made, shall be punished with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to one month, or with fine which may extend to five hundred rupees, or with both; or, if the summons, notice, order or proclamation is to attend in person or by agent, or (to produce a document or electronic record in a Court of Justice) with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both.

174.title: Non-attendance in obedience to an order from public servant
174.what: Intentionally failing to attend at a place and time when legally required to do so, or leaving before the allowed departure time, can result in imprisonment for up to 6 months, fine of up to ₹1,000, or both.

174A.title: Non-appearance in response to a proclamation under section 82 of Act 2 of 1974
174A.what: If you don't appear at the place and time specified in a proclamation made under section 82 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, you can be punished with up to 3 years in prison or a fine, or both. If you've already been declared a 'proclaimed offender', you can face up to 7 years in prison and a fine.

175.title: Omission to produce document to public servant by person legally bound to produce it
175.what: A person who is legally required to produce or deliver a document to a public servant intentionally fails to do so, and may face imprisonment for up to one month or a fine of up to five hundred rupees, or both.

176.title: Omission to give notice or information to public servant by person legally bound to give it
176.what: A person who is legally required to give notice or information to a public servant intentionally fails to do so may face imprisonment for up to 6 months, or a fine of up to ₹1,000, or both.

177.title: Furnishing false information
177.what: Whoever, being legally bound to furnish information on any subject to any public servant, as such, furnishes false information on the subject which he knows or has reason to believe to be false shall be punished with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both; or, if the information which he is legally bound to give respects the commission of an offence, or is required for the purpose of preventing the commission of an offence, or in order to the apprehension of an offender, with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.

178.title: Refusing oath or affirmation when duly required by public servant to make it
178.what: Refusing to take an oath or affirmation when required by a public servant to do so, and failing to state the truth, can result in imprisonment for up to 6 months, a fine of up to ₹1,000, or both.

179.title: Refusing to answer public servant authorised to question
179.what: Whoever, being legally bound to state the truth on any subject to any public servant, refuses to answer any question demanded of him touching that subject by such public servant in the exercise of the legal powers of such public servant, shall be punished with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both.

180.title: Refusing to sign statement
180.what: If someone is asked by a public servant to sign a statement and they refuse, they can face punishment such as imprisonment for up to 3 months, a fine of up to 500 rupees, or both.

181.title: False statement on oath or affirmation to public servant or person authorised to administer
181.what: Making a false statement on oath or affirmation to a public servant or authorized person is punishable by up to 3 years in prison and a fine.

182.title: False information, with intent to cause public servant to use his lawful power to the injury
182.what: A person intentionally gives false information to a public servant, knowing it may cause harm, and the public servant uses their power to cause harm to someone else.

183.title: Resistance to the taking of property by the lawful authority of a public servant
183.what: A person who knows they are being taken property by a government official and resists will face up to 6 months in jail, a fine of up to 1000 rupees, or both.

184.title: Obstructing sale of property offered for sale b y authority of publ ic servant
184.what: A person intentionally blocking the sale of property sold by a government official can face up to 1 month in jail, a fine of up to ₹500, or both.

185.title: Illegal purchase or bid for property offered for sale b y authority of public servant
185.what: Whoever, at any sale of property held by the lawful authority of a public servant, as such, purchases or bids for any property on account of any person, whether himself or any other, whom he knows to be under a legal incapacity to purchase that property at that sale, or bids for such property not intending to perform the obligations under which he lays himself by such bidding, shall be punished with imprisonment of either 1. 186.title: Obstructing public servant in discharge of public functions
186.what: A person who intentionally blocks a government official doing their job can get up to 3 months in jail, or be fined up to ₹500, or both.

187.title: Omission to assist public servant when bo und by law to give assistance
187.what: A person who is legally required to assist a public servant in their duties intentionally fails to do so can face punishment including up to 6 months imprisonment, a fine of up to ₹500, or both.

188.title: Disobedience to order duly p romulgated by public servant
188.what: Disobedience to an order duly promulgated by a public servant can result in punishment with imprisonment for up to 6 months or fine of up to ₹1,000, depending on the severity of the harm caused.

189.title: Threa t of injury to public servant
189.what: Threatening injury to public servant to influence their actions

190.title: Threat of injury to induce person to refrain from applying for protection to public servant
190.what: Threatening someone to stop them from applying for protection against an injury to a public servant, in order to prevent the person from making a legal application.

191.title: Giving false evidence
191.what: Whoever, being legally bound by an oath or by an express provision of law to state the truth, makes any statement which is false, and which he either knows or believes to be false or does not believe to be true, is said to give false evidence.

192.title: Fabricating false evidence
192.what: Fabricating false evidence means intentionally creating or altering information to influence the outcome of a court case or other official proceeding, with the goal of causing someone to form an incorrect opinion about the facts.

193.title: Punishment for false evidence
193.what: Whoever intentionally gives false evidence in any judicial proceeding or fabricates false evidence for use in a judicial proceeding shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term that may extend to seven years and shall also be liable to fine. Whoever intentionally gives or fabricates false evidence in any other case shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term that may extend to three years and shall also be liable to fine.

194.title: Giving or fabricating false evidence with intent to procure conviction of capital offence
194.what: Giving or fabricating false evidence with intent to procure conviction of capital offence. Whoever gives or fabricates false evidence intending thereby to cause any person to be convicted of an offence which is capital by the law for the time being in force in India shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or with rigorous imprisonment for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.

195.title: Giving or fabricating false evidence with intent to procure conviction of offence punishable
195.what: Giving false evidence with intent to cause conviction of an offence punishable with imprisonment for life or seven years or more.

195A.title: Threatening any person to give false evidence
195A.what: Threatening someone to give false testimony can lead to imprisonment of up to 7 years or a fine, or both. If an innocent person is wrongly convicted due to this threat, the person who threatened will face the same punishment as the innocent person.

196.title: Using evidence known to be false
196.what: Whoever corruptly uses or attempts to use as true or genuine evidence any evidence which he knows to be false or fabricated, shall be punished.

197.title: Issuing or signing false certificate
197.what: Issuing or signing a false certificate can lead to punishment for giving false evidence.

198.title: Using as true a certificate known to be false
198.what: Using as true a certificate known to be false: Whoever corruptly uses or attempts to use any such certificate as a true certificate, knowing the same to be false in any material point, shall be punished in the same manner as if he gave false evidence.

199.title: False statement made in declaration which is by law receivable as evidence
199.what: Whoever, in any declaration made or subscribed by him, which declaration an y Court of Justice, or any public servant or other person, is bound or authori sed by law to receive as evidence of any fact, makes any statement which is false, and which he either knows or believes to be false or does not believe to be true, touching any point material to the object for which the declaration is made or used, shall be punished in the same manner as if he gave false evidence.

200.title: Using as true such declaration knowing it to be false
200.what: Whoever corruptly uses or attempts to use as true any such declaration, knowing the same to be false in any material point, shall be punished in the same manner as if he gave false evidence. Explanation.—A declaration which is inadmissible merely upon the ground of some informality, is a declaration within the meaning of sections 199 and 200.

201.title: Causing disappearance of evidence of offence, or giving false information to screen
201.what: offender.—Whoever, knowing or having reason to believe that an offence has been committed, causes any evidence of the commission of that offence to disappear, with the intention of screening the offender from legal punishment, or with that intention gives any information respecting the offence which he knows or believes to be false, if a capital offence .—shall, if the offence which he kno ws or believes to have been com mitted is punishable with death be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine; if punishable with imprisonment for life.—and if the offence is punishable with 1[imprisonment for life], or with imprisonment which may extend to ten years, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, and shall also be liable to fine; if punishable with less t han ten years ’ imprisonment .—and if the offence is punishable with imprisonment for any term not extending to ten years, shall be punished with imprisonment of the description provided for the offence, for a term which may extend to one-fourth part of the longest term of the imprisonment provided for the offence, or with fine, or with both. Illustration A, knowing that B has murdered Z, assists B to hide the body with the intention of screening B from punishment. A is liable to imprisonment of either description for seven years, and also to fine.

202.title: Intentional omission to give information of offe nce by person bound to inform
202.what: Whoever, knowing or having reason to believe that an offence has been committed, intentionally omits to give any information respecting that offence which he is legally bound to give, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine, or with both.

203.title: Giving false information res pecting an offence committed
203.what: Whoever, knowing or having reason to believe that an offence has been committed, gives any information respecting that offence which he knows or believes to be false, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both. 204.title: Destruction of document to prevent its production as evidence
204.what: Whoever secretes or destroys any 3[document and electronic record] which he may be lawfully compelled to produce as evidence in a Court of Justice, or in any proceeding lawfully held before a public servant, as such, or obliterates or renders illegible the whole or any part of such 3[document or electronic record] with the intention of preventing the same from being produced or used as evidence before such Court or public servant as aforesaid, or after he shall have been lawfully summoned or required to produce the same for that purpose, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two yea rs, or with fine, or with both.

205.title: False personation for purpose of act or proceeding in suit or prosecution
205.what: Whoever falsely personates another, and in such assumed character makes any admission or stat ement, or confesses judgment, or causes any process to be issued or becomes bail or security, or does any other act in any suit or criminal prosecution, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both.

206.title: Fraudulent removal or concealment of property to prevent its seizure as forfeited or in
206.what: Whoever fraudulently removes, conceals, transfers or delivers to any person any property or any interest therein, intending t hereby to prevent that property or interest therein from being taken as a forfeiture or in

207.title: Fraudulent claim to property to prevent its seizure as forfeited or in execution
207.what: Whoever fraudulently accepts, receives or claims any property or any interest therein, knowing that he has no right or rightful claim to such property or interest, or practices any deception touching any right to any property or any interest therein, intending thereby to prevent that property or interest therein from being taken as a forfeiture or in satisfaction of a fine, under a sentence which has been pronounced, or which he knows to be likely to be pronounced by a Court of Justice or other competent authority, or from being taken in execution of a decree or order which has been made, or which he knows to be likely to be made by a Court of Justice in a civil suit, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.

208.title: Fraudulently suffering decree for sum not due
208.what: Fraudulently causing or suffering a decree to be passed against you for a sum not due, a larger sum than you are entitled to, or for property you don't own, and then having it executed after it's been satisfied, can result in imprisonment of up to 2 years, a fine, or both.

209.title: Dishonesty making false claim in Court
209.what: Making a false claim in court with intent to injure or annoy someone, knowing it is false, can lead to up to 2 years in prison and a fine.

210.title: Fraudulently obtaining decree for sum not due
210.what: Fraudulently obtaining a decree or order for a sum not due, or for a larger sum than is due, or for any property or interest in property to which he is not entitled.

211.title: False charge of offenc e made with intent to injure
211.what: Whoever institutes or causes a criminal proceeding against a person with intent to cause injury, falsely charges a person with an offence knowing there is no just ground for it, shall be punished with imprisonment up to 2 years or fine or both.

212.title: Harbouring offender
212.what: Harbouring or concealing an offender with the intention of screening him from legal punishment.

213.title: Taking gift, etc., to scre en an offender from punishment
213.what: Whoever accepts or attempts to obtain, or agrees to accept, any gratification for himself or any other person, or any restitution of property to himself or any other person, in consideration of his concealing an offence or of his screening any person from legal punishment for any offence, or of his not proceeding against any person for the purpose of bringing him to legal punishment, if a capital offence.—shall, if the offence is punishable with death, be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine; if punishable with imprisonment for life, or with imprisonment.—and if the offence is punishable with 3[imprisonment for life], or with imprisonment which may extend to ten years, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which m ay extend to three years, and shall als o be liable to fine; and if the offence is punishable with imprisonment not extending to ten years, shall be punished with imprisonment of the description provided for the offence for a term which may extend to one fourth part of the longest term of imprisonment provided for the offence, or with fine, or with both.

214.title: Offering gift or restoration of property in consideration of screening offender
214.what: Offers a gift or restores property in exchange for concealing an offense, screening someone from punishment, or not prosecuting someone.

215.title: Taking gift to help to recover stolen property, etc
215.what: Taking gift to help recover stolen property: If you accept a gift to help find someone who stole your property, but don't try to catch the thief, you can be punished with up to 2 years in prison, a fine, or both.

216.title: Harbouring offender who has escaped from custody or whose apprehension has been
216.what: harbouring or concealing a person who has escaped from custody or whose apprehension has been ordered, with the intention of preventing them from being apprehended.

216A.title: Penalty for harbouring robbers or dacoits
216A.what: Whoever, knowing or having reason to believe that any persons are about to commit or have recently committed robbery or dacoity, harbours them or any of them, with the intention of facilitating the commission of such robbery or dacoity, or of screening them or any of them from punishment, shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.

217.title: Public servant disobeying direct ion of law with intent to save person from punishmen t or
217.what: A public servant intentionally disobeys the law to save someone from punishment or property from being forfeited.

218.title: Public servant framing incorrect record or writing with intent to save perso n from
218.what: A public servant intentionally creates an incorrect record or writing that could cause harm to the public or someone, or tries to save someone from punishment, and this is done with the intention of saving property from a legal penalty.

219.title: Public servant in judicial proceeding corruptly making report, etc., contrary to law
219.what: A public servant who corruptly makes or pronounces a report, order, verdict, or decision in a judicial proceeding that is against the law will be punished with imprisonment for up to 7 years, or a fine, or both.

220.title: Commitment for trial or confinement by person having authority who knows that he is acting
220.what: A person who has authority to commit someone for trial or confinement and knowingly acts against the law while doing so will face punishment.

221.title: Intentional omissio n to apprehend on the part of publ ic servant bound to apprehend
221.what: A public servant intentionally fails to apprehend someone, allows them to escape, or helps them escape from confinement. This is punishable by: - Up to 7 years in prison and/or fine if the person was charged with an offence punishable by death. - Up to 3 years in prison and/or fine if the person was charged with an offence punishable by life imprisonment or up to 10 years in prison. - Up to 2 years in prison and/or fine if the person was charged with an offence punishable by less than 10 years in prison.

222.title: Intentional omission to apprehend on the part of public servant bound to apprehend person
222.what: A public servant who is legally bound to apprehend or keep in confinement someone under court order intentionally fails to do so, aids them in escaping, or allows them to escape. They may face imprisonment for life, up to 14 years, or up to 7 years with a fine, depending on the severity of the sentence.

223.title: Escape from confinement or custody negligently suffered by public servant
223.what: Whoever, being a public servant legally bound as such public servant to keep in confinement any person charged with or convicted of any offence, negligently suffers such person to escape from confinement, shall be punished with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.

224.title: Resistance or obstruction by a pers on to his lawful apprehension
224.what: A person who resists arrest, interferes with their lawful detention, or tries to escape will face up to 2 years in prison, a fine, or both.

225.title: Resistance or obstruction to lawful apprehension of another person
225.what: Resisting or obstructing lawful apprehension of another person for an offence, rescuing or attempting to rescue someone from lawful custody, and punishment terms

225A.title: Omission to apprehend, or s ufferance of escape, on part of public servant, in cases not
225A.what: If a public servant fails to apprehend or allows an escape of a person in a case not covered by other laws, they can be punished. If it's intentional, the punishment is up to 3 years imprisonment or fine. If it's negligent, the punishment is up to 2 years imprisonment or fine.

225B.title: Resistance or obstruction to lawful apprehension, or escape or rescue in cases not otherwise
225B.what: Intentionally offers resistance or obstruction to lawful apprehension, escapes from custody, rescues someone from custody, or attempts to do so.

227.title: Violation of condition of remission of punishment
227.what: If you accept a reduced sentence, but break the conditions, you'll get the original sentence. If you've already served some of it, you'll get the remaining amount.

228.title: Intentional insult or interruption to public servant sitting in judicial proceeding
228.what: A person who intentionally insults or interrupts a public servant during a court hearing can face up to 6 months in jail, a fine of up to ₹1,000, or both.

228A.title: Disclosure of identity of the victim of certain offences, etc

229.title: Personation of a juror or assessor
229.what: Intentionally pretending to be a juror or assessor when not legally allowed, and serving anyway, can result in up to 2 years in prison, a fine, or both.

229A.title: Failure by person released on bail or bond to appear in court

230.title: “Coin” defined
230.what: Coin is metal used for the time being as money, and stamped and issued by the authority of some State or Sovereign Power in order to be so used.

231.title: Counterfeiting coin
231.what: Counterfeiting coin: Counterfeiting or knowingly performing part of counterfeiting process can lead to up to 7 years imprisonment and fine.

232.title: Counterfeiting Indian coin
232.what: Counterfeiting Indian coin: Punishment - Imprisonment for life or up to 10 years and fine

233.title: Making or selling instrument for counterfeiting coin
233.what: Section 233 states that whoever makes or mends, or performs any part of the process of making or mending, or buys, sells or disposes of, any die or instrument for the purpose of being used, or knowing or having reason to believe that it is intended to be used, for the purpose of counterfeiting coin shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, and shall also be liable to fine.

234.title: Making or selling instrument f or counterfeiting Indian coin
234.what: Making or selling instrument for counterfeiting Indian coin shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.

235.title: Possession of instrument or material for the purpose of using the same for counterfeiting
235.what: Possession of an instrument or material for the purpose of using it to counterfeit coins can lead to up to 3 years in prison and/or a fine. If the counterfeited coin is Indian currency, the punishment can be up to 10 years in prison and/or a fine.

236.title: Abetting in India the counterfeiting out of India of coin
236.what: Abetting the counterfeiting of coin outside India, with punishment equal to abetting it inside India.

237.title: Import or export of counterfeit coin
237.what: Importing or exporting counterfeit coins into/out of India can lead to up to 3 years in prison and a fine.

238.title: Import or export of counterfeits of the Indian coin
238.what: Imports or exports counterfeits of Indian coins. If someone brings in or takes out counterfeit Indian coin they can get up to 10 years in prison and/or a fine.

239.title: Delivery of coin , possessed with knowledge that it is counterfeit
239.what: A person who knowingly possesses counterfeit coin will be punished if they deliver it to someone or try to get them to take it.

240.title: Delivery of Indian coin, possessed with kno wledge that it is counterfeit
240.what: A person who knowingly possesses counterfeit Indian coins and delivers them fraudulently will face up to 10 years in prison and a fine.

241.title: Delivery of coin as genuine, which, when first possessed, the deliverer d id not know to be
241.what: Delivering a known counterfeit coin as genuine, without knowing it was counterfeit when first possessed.

242.title: Possession of counterfeit coin by person who knew it to be counterfeit whe n he became
242.what: Possession of counterfeit coin by person who knew it to be counterfeit when he became possessed thereof.—Whoever, fraudulently or with intent that fraud may be committed, is in possession of counterfeit coin, having known at the time when he became possessed thereof that such coin was counterfeit, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, and shall also be liable to fine.

243.title: Possession of Indian coin by person who knew it to be counterfeit when he became possessed
243.what: A person who knowingly possesses counterfeit Indian coins with the intention of committing fraud will face up to 7 years in prison and a fine.

244.title: Person employed in mint causing coin to be of different weight or compo sition from that
244.what: Causing coins to have incorrect weight or composition while employed at a mint.

245.title: Unlawfully taking coining instrument from mint
245.what: Taking a coining instrument from a mint without authority

246.title: Fraudulently or dishonestly diminishing weight or altering composition of coin
246.what: Fraudulently or dishonestly diminishing weight or altering composition of coin: Whoever performs any operation on a coin that diminishes its weight or alters its composition, shall be punished with up to 3 years imprisonment and a fine.

247.title: Fraudulently or dishonestly diminishin g weight or alteri ng composition of Indian coin
247.what: Fraudulently or dishonestly diminishing the weight or altering the composition of Indian coins will result in up to 7 years of imprisonment and a fine.

248.title: Altering appearance of coin with intent that it shall pass as coin of different description
248.what: A person who changes the appearance of a coin on purpose so it looks like a different type of coin will get up to 3 years in prison and have to pay a fine.

249.title: Altering appearance of Indian coin with intent that it shall pass a s coin of different
249.what: A person who alters the appearance of an Indian coin with the intention that it will pass as a different type of coin can be punished with imprisonment for up to 7 years and a fine.

250.title: Delivery of coin , possessed with knowledge that it is altered
250.what: Delivering altered coin with knowledge that it is altered

251.title: Delivery of Indian coin, possessed with knowledge that it is altered
251.what: Delivering Indian coin that you know has been altered with intent to commit fraud or knowing it's altered, can lead to up to 10 years in prison and a fine.

252.title: Possession of coin by person who knew it to be altered when he became possessed thereof
252.what: Possession of altered coin by person who knew it was altered

253.title: Possession of Indian coin by person who knew it to be altered whe n he became possessed
253.what: A person who knowingly has possession of altered Indian coins with the intention of committing fraud or allowing others to commit fraud will face up to 5 years in prison and a fine.

254.title: Delivery of coin as genuine which, when first possessed, the deliver er did not know to be
254.what: Delivers a counterfeit coin that they did not know was altered when they first possessed it.

255.title: Counterfeiting Government stamp
255.what: Counterfeiting Government stamp: Counterfeiting or knowingly performing part of the process of counterfeiting government revenue stamps will result in imprisonment for life or up to 10 years, and a fine.

256.title: Having possession of instrument or material for co unterfeiting Gov ernment stamp
256.what: Possession of instrument or material for counterfeiting government stamps can lead to up to 7 years imprisonment and fine.

257.title: Making or selling instrument for co unterfeiting Government stamp
257.what: Making or selling an instrument for counterfeiting Government stamps can result in imprisonment for up to 7 years and a fine.

258.title: Sale of counterfeit Government stamp
258.what: Selling counterfeit government stamps can lead to up to 7 years in prison and a fine.
