259.title: Having posses sion of counterfeit Government stamp
259.what: Possessing counterfeit government stamp with intent to use or dispose of it as genuine, punishable by up to 7 years imprisonment and fine.

260.title: Using as genuine a Government stamp known to be counterfeit
260.what: Using as genuine a Government stamp known to be counterfeit

261.title: Effacing writing from substance bearing Government stamp, or removing from document a
261.what: Removes or effaces government stamp from substance or document with intent to cause loss to Government

262.title: Using Government stamp kn own to have been before used
262.what: Using a government stamp that has already been used fraudulently or to cause loss to the Government.

263.title: Erasure of mark denoting that stamp has been used
263.what: Erasing or removing a mark from a government stamp that indicates it has been used is punishable by up to 3 years in prison, or a fine, or both.

263A.title: Prohibition of fictitious stamps
263A.what: Making, uttering, dealing in, selling, or using fictitious stamps is punishable with a fine of up to Rs. 200

264.title: Fraudulent use of false instrument for weighing
264.what: A person who knowingly uses a fake weight-measuring device will face up to 1 year in prison, or a fine, or both.

265.title: Fraudulent use of false weight or measure
265.what: Whoever, fraudulently uses any false weight or false measure of length or capacity, or fraudulently uses any weight or any measure of length or capacity as a different weight or measure from what it is, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine, or with both.

266.title: Being in possession of false weight or measure
266.what: Possessing an instrument with false weight or measure with intent to use it fraudulently.

267.title: Making or se lling false weight or measure
267.what: Making or selling false weight or measure

268.title: Public nuisance
268.what: A person is guilty of a public nuisance if their act or omission causes harm to the general public, people in nearby properties, or those who may need to use public rights.

269.title: Negligent act likely to spread infection of disease dangerous to life
269.what: A person who intentionally or negligently spreads an infectious disease that can cause serious harm to life will face imprisonment for up to 6 months, or a fine, or both.

270.title: Malignant act likely to spread infection of di sease dangerous to life
270.what: A person who intentionally does an act that could spread a serious illness and cause harm to someone's life will face up to 2 years in prison, a fine, or both.

271.title: Di sobedience to quarantine rule
271.what: A person who knowingly disobeys quarantine rules and regulations can be punished with: imprisonment for up to 6 months, fine, or both.

272.title: Adulteration of f ood or drink intende d for sale
272.what: Adultering any article of food or drink so it becomes noxious and selling it as food or drink, can lead to imprisonment up to 6 months, a fine of up to ₹1000, or both.

273.title: Sale of noxious food or drink
273.what: Selling noxious food or drink is punishable with imprisonment up to 6 months or fine up to Rs. 1000 or both.

274.title: Adulteration of drugs
274.what: Adulterating drugs for medicinal purposes can lead to imprisonment up to 6 months or fine up to Rs. 1000 or both.

275.title: Sale of adulterated drugs
275.what: Selling adulterated drugs is punishable with imprisonment up to 6 months or fine up to Rs. 1000 or both.

276.title: Sale of drug as a different drug or preparation
276.what: Misrepresenting a drug as a different one can lead to imprisonment up to 6 months or fine up to Rs. 1000 or both.

277.title: Fouling water of public spring or reservoir
277.what: Polluting public water sources can result in imprisonment up to 3 months or fine up to Rs. 500 or both.

278.title: Making atmosphere noxious to h ealth
278.what: Making the atmosphere noxious can lead to a fine of up to Rs. 500.

279.title: Rash driving or riding on a public way
279.what: Rash driving on public ways is punishable with imprisonment up to 6 months or fine up to Rs. 1000 or both.

280.title: Rash navigation of vessel
280.what: Rash navigation of vessels can result in imprisonment up to 6 months or fine up to Rs. 1000 or both.

281.title: Exhibition of false light, mark or buoy
281.what: Exhibiting false light, mark or buoy intending to mislead navigators is punishable with imprisonment of up to 7 years or fine.

282.title: Conveying person by water for hire in unsafe or overloaded vessel
282.what: Conveying a person by water for hire in an unsafe or overloaded vessel is punishable with imprisonment up to 6 months, or a fine of up to ₹1,000, or both.

283.title: Danger or obstruction in public way or line of navigation
283.what: Causing danger, obstruction, or injury to a person in a public way or line of navigation by doing an act or failing to take care of property.

284.title: Negligent conduct with respect to poisonous substance
284.what: A person who handles a poisonous substance in a careless way that could harm someone's life or cause injury will be punished.

285.title: Negligent conduct with respect to fire or combustible matter
285.what: Whoever does, with fire or any combustible matter, any act so rashly or negligently as to endanger human life, or to be likely to cause hurt or injury to any other person, or knowingly or negligently omits to take such order with any fire or any combustible matter in his possession as is sufficient to guard against any probable danger to human life from such fire or combustible matter.

286.title: Negligent conduct with re spect to explosive substance
286.what: Whoever does, with any explosive substance, any act so rashly or negligently as to endanger human life, or to be likely to cause hurt or injury to any other person, or knowingly or negligently omits to take such order with any explosive substance in his possession as is sufficient to guard against any probable danger to human life from that substance.

287.title: Negligent conduct with respect to machinery
287.what: Whoever does, with any machinery, any act so rashly or negligently as to endanger human life or to be likely to cause hurt or injury to any other person, or knowingly or negligently omits to take such order with any machinery in his possession or under his care as is sufficient to guard against any probable danger to human life from such machinery.

288.title: Negligent conduct with respect to pulling down or repairing buildings
288.what: A person who knowingly or negligently fails to take necessary precautions to prevent harm from the collapse of a building during demolition or repair can be punished with imprisonment for up to 6 months, a fine of up to ₹1,000, or both.

289.title: Negligent conduct with respect to animal
289.what: Knowingly or negligently omitting to take order to guard against probable danger from animal

290.title: Punishment for public nuisance in ca ses not otherwise provided for
290.what: A person who creates a public nuisance that is not specifically punished under the Indian Penal Code 1860 can be fined up to ₹200.

291.title: Continuance of nuisance aft er injunction to discontinue
291.what: If someone continues a public nuisance after being told not to by a government official, they can get up to 6 months in jail, or a fine, or both.

292.title: Sale, etc., of obscene books, etc
292.what: Section 292 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860, deals with the sale, distribution, or possession of obscene books, pamphlets, papers, circulars, or any other written matter which is likely to corrupt public morals. The section states that whoever publishes, sells, circulates, or distributes such obscene material, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, and shall also be liable to fine.

293.title: Sale, etc., of obs cene objects to young person
293.what: Selling obscene objects to young persons is punishable with imprisonment up to 3 years and a fine of up to Rs 2000.

294.title: Obscene acts and songs
294.what: A person can be punished with up to 3 months' imprisonment, or a fine, or both if they perform an obscene act in public or sing/utter obscene words in a public place.

294A.title: Keeping lottery office
294A.what: Keeping an office for drawing a lottery (except state lottery) can lead to imprisonment of up to 6 months or a fine, and publishing lottery proposals can result in a fine of up to ₹1000.

295.title: Injuring or defiling place of worship, with intent to insult the religion of any class
295.what: Whoever destroys, damages or defiles any place of worship, or any object held sacred by any class of persons with the intention of insulting their religion, shall be punished with imprisonment for up to 2 years, or a fine, or both.

295A.title: Del iberate and malicious acts , intended to outrage religious feelings of any class by
295A.what: Deliberate and malicious acts intended to outrage religious feelings of any class by insulting its religion or religious beliefs.

296.title: Disturbing religious assembly
296.what: A person who intentionally disrupts a group of people who are legally attending a religious service can be imprisoned for up to 1 year, fined, or both.

297.title: Trespassing on burial places, etc
297.what: Trespassing on burial places, etc. - Punishment: Imprisonment of up to 1 year, fine, or both, if the intention is to wound feelings, insult religion, or cause disturbance during funeral ceremonies.

298.title: Uttering words, etc., with deliberate inten t to wound religious feelings
298.what: Uttering words, making sounds, or gestures with the intention of wounding someone's religious feelings can lead to imprisonment for up to 1 year, a fine, or both.

299.title: Culpable homicide
299.what: Whoever causes death by doing an act with the intention of causing death, or with the intention of causing such bodily injury as is likely to cause death, or with the knowledge that he is likely by such act to cause death, commits the offence of culpable homicide.

300.title: Murder
300.what: Section 300 states that culpable homicide is murder if the act by which the death is caused is done with the intention of causing death or bodily injury as the offender knows to be likely to cause the death of the person to whom the harm is caused.

301.title: Culpable homicide by causing death of person other than pe rson whose death was
301.what: If a person, by doing anything which he intends or knows to be likely to cause death, commits culpable homicide by causing the death of any person, whose death he neither intends nor knows himself to be likely to cause, the culpable homicide committed by the offender is of the description of which it would have been if he had caused the death of the person who se death he intended or knew himself to he likely to cause.

302.title: Punishment for murder
302.what: A person who kills someone will be punished with either death, imprisonment for life, or a fine.

303.title: Punishment for murder by life-convict
303.what: If someone who is already serving a life sentence (imprisonment for life) kills someone else, they will receive the death penalty.

304.title: Punishment for culpable homi cide not amounting to murder
304.what: A person who causes the death of another person through culpable homicide not amounting to murder can be punished with imprisonment for life, or up to 10 years in prison, and/or a fine, if they intended to cause death or serious injury, or if they knew their actions could cause death but did not intend to.

304A.title: Causing death by negligence
304A.what: Causing death by negligence. Whoever causes the death of any person by doing any rash or negligent act not amounting to culpable homicide , shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.

304B.title: Dowry death
304B.what: A woman's death is considered 'dowry death' if she dies due to burns or injuries within 7 years of marriage, and was subjected to cruelty or harassment by her husband or relative before her death, related to dowry demands.

305.title: Abetment of suicide of child or insane person
305.what: A person who helps someone else commit suicide will be punished with either death, life imprisonment, or up to 10 years in prison, and may also have to pay a fine.

306.title: Abetment of suicide
306.what: A person who helps someone else commit suicide can get up to 10 years in prison and a fine.

307.title: Attempt to murder
307.what: Attempt to murder: Whoever does any act with intention or knowledge, and under circumstances that would make them guilty of murder if death resulted, shall be punished with up to 10 years imprisonment and/or fine. If someone is hurt, they may get life imprisonment or the original punishment.

308.title: Attemp t to commit c ulpable homicide

309.title: Attempt to commit suicide
309.what: A person who tries to kill themselves and takes actions to do so will get up to 1 year in jail, or a fine, or both.

310.title: Thug
310.what: A person who has often worked with others to commit robbery or kidnapping with murder is considered a thug.

311.title: Punishment
311.what: A person who is a thug can be punished with imprisonment for life and fined.

312.title: Causing miscarraige
312.what: Causing miscarriage: A person intentionally causing a woman with child to miscarry can be punished with imprisonment up to 3 years or fine (or both), and if the woman is pregnant, punishment can be up to 7 years in prison and fine.

313.title: Causing miscarriage without woman's consent
313.what: Causing miscarriage without the woman's consent is punishable by imprisonment for life or up to 10 years, and/or fine.

314.title: Death caused by act done with intent to cause miscarriage
314.what: A person who intentionally causes a woman's death while trying to induce a miscarriage will face up to 10 years in prison and a fine.

315.title: Act done with inten t to prevent child being born alive or t o cause it to die after birth
315.what: Whoever before the birth of any child does any act with the intention of thereby preventing that child from being born alive or causing it to die after its birth, and does by such act prevent that child from being born alive, or causes it to die after its birth, shall, if such act be not caused in good faith for the purpose of saving the life of the mother, be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, or with fine, or with both.

316.title: Causing death of quick unborn child by act amounting to culpable homicide
316.what: Causing death of a quick unborn child by an act that would be considered culpable homicide if it resulted in the death of a person, shall result in imprisonment for up to 10 years and/or fine.

317.title: Exposure and abandonment of child under twelve years, by parent or person having care of
317.what: Exposing or leaving a child under 12 years old with the intention of abandoning it can result in imprisonment for up to 7 years, or a fine, or both.

318.title: Concealment of birth by secret disposal of dead body
318.what: Intentionally concealing the birth of a child by secretly burying or disposing of its dead body.

319.title: Hurt
319.what: Causing bodily pain, disease or infirmity to another person results in physical harm.

320.title: Grievous hurt
320.what: complete explanation of grievous hurt includes: emasculation, permanent loss of sight or hearing, privation of a member or joint, destruction of powers of a member or joint, permanent disfiguration of the head or face, fracture or dislocation of a bone or tooth, and any hurt that endangers life or causes severe bodily pain for 20 days.

321.title: Voluntarily causing hurt
321.what: A person intentionally causes harm to another person, or knows they may be harmed, and actually causes harm.

322.title: Volu ntarily causing grievous hurt
322.what: A person intentionally or knowingly causes grievous hurt and also intends or knows they are likely to cause a different kind of grievous hurt.

323.title: Punishment for voluntarily causing hurt
323.what: Punishment for voluntarily causing hurt, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both.

324.title: Voluntarily causing hurt b y dangerous weapons or means
324.what: Voluntarily causing hurt by using dangerous weapons or means, such as shooting, stabbing, fire, poison, or explosives, can lead to imprisonment for up to 3 years or a fine.

325.title: Punishment for voluntarily causing grievous hurt
325.what: Voluntarily causing grievous hurt: Imprisonment up to 7 years and fine

326.title: Voluntarily causing grievous hurt by dangerous weapons or means
326.what: Voluntarily causing grievous hurt by using dangerous weapons or means, such as fire, poison, explosives, or substances harmful to the human body.

326A.title: Voluntarily causing grievous hurt by use of acid, etc
326A.what: Voluntarily causing grievous hurt by use of acid, etc. - Whoever causes permanent or partial damage or deformity to, or burns or maims or disfigures or disables, any part or parts of the body of a person or causes grievous hurt by throwing acid on or by administering acid to that person, or by using any other means with the intention of causing or with the knowledge that he is likely to cause such injury or hurt, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which shall not be less than ten years but which may extend to imprisonment for life, and with fine.

326B.title: Voluntarily throwing or attempting to throw acid
326B.what: Voluntarily throwing or attempting to throw acid on a person with the intention of causing permanent or partial damage, burns, maiming, disfigurement, disability, or grievous hurt.

327.title: Voluntarily causing hurt to extort property, or to constrain to an illegal to an act
327.what: A person who intentionally causes harm to someone in order to get money or property from them, or to force them to do something illegal, can face up to 10 years in prison and a fine.

328.title: Causing hurt by means of poison, etc., with intent to commit and offence
328.what: Administering poison or intoxicating substance with intent to cause harm or commit an offence

329.title: Voluntarily causing grievous hurt to extort property, or to constrain to an illegal act
329.what: Whoever voluntarily causes grievous hurt for the purpose of extorting from the sufferer or from any person interested in the sufferer any property or valuable security, or of constraining the sufferer or any person interested in such sufferer to do anything that is illegal or which may facilitate the commission of an offence, shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.

330.title: Voluntarily causing hurt to extort confession , or to compel restoration of property
330.what: Whoever voluntarily causes hurt, for the purpose of extorting from the sufferer or from any person interested in the sufferer, any confession or any information which may lead to the detection of an offence or misconduct, or for the purpose o f constraining the sufferer or any person interested in the sufferer to restore or to cause the restoration of any property or valuable security or to satisfy any claim or demand, or to give information which may lead to the restoration of any property or valuable security, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.

331.title: Voluntarily causing griev ous hurt to extort confession, or to c ompel restoration of
331.what: Whoever voluntarily causes grievous hurt for the purpose of extorting from the sufferer or from any person interested in the sufferer any confession or any information which may lead to the detection of an offence or misconduct, or for the purpose of constrai ning the sufferer or any person interested in the sufferer to restore or to cause the restoration of any property or valuable security, or to satisfy any claim or demand or to give information which may lead to the restoration of any property or valuable security, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, an d shall also be liable to fine.

332.title: Voluntarily causing hurt to deter public servant from his duty
332.what: Whoever voluntarily causes hurt to any person being a public servant in the discharge of his duty as such public servant, or with intent to prevent or deter that person or any other public servant from discharging his duty as such public servant or in consequence of anything done or attempted to be done by that person in the lawful discharge of his duty as such public servant, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both.

333.title: Voluntarily causing grievous hurt to deter public servant from his duty
333.what: Whoever voluntarily causes grievous hurt to any person being a pub lic servant in the discharge of his duty as such public servant, or with intent to prevent or deter that person or any other public servant from discharging his duty as such public servant, or in consequence of anything done or attempted to be done by that person in the lawful discharge of his duty as such public servant, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.

334.title: Voluntaril y causing hurt on provocation
334.what: Whoever voluntarily causes hurt on grave and sudden provocation, if he neither intends nor knows himself to be likely to cause hurt to any person other than the person who gave the provocation, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one month, or with fine which may extend to five hundred rupees, or with both.

335.title: Voluntarily causing grievous hurt on provocation
335.what: Whoever 1[voluntarily] causes grievous hurt on grave and sudden provocation, if he neither intends nor knows himself to be likely to cause grievous hurt to any person other than the person who gave the provocation, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to four years, or with fine which may extend to two thousand rupees, or with both.

336.title: Act endangering life or personal safety of others
336.what: Whoever does any act so rashly or negligently as to endanger human life or the personal safety of others, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three months or with fine which may extend to two hundred and fifty rupees, or with both.

337.title: Causing hurt by act endangering life o r personal safety of others
337.what: Causing hurt by act endangering life o r personal safety of others: Whoever causes hurt to any person by doing any act so rashly or negligently as to endanger human life, or the personal safety of others, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to five hundred rupees, or with both.

338.title: Causing grievous hurt by act endangering life or personal safety of others
338.what: Causing grievous hurt by act endangering life or personal safety of others: Whoever causes grievous hurt to any person by doing any act so rashly or negligently as to endanger human life, or the personal safety of others, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both. Of wrongful restraint and wrongful confinement

339.title: Wrongful restraint
339.what: Wrongful restraint: Whoever voluntarily obstructs any person so as to prevent that person from proceeding in any direction in which that person has a right to proceed, is said wrongfully to restrain that person. Exception.—The obstruction of a private way over land or water which a person in good faith believes himself to have a lawful right to obstruct, is not an offence within the meaning of this section. Illustration A obstructs a path along which Z has a right to pass, A not believing in good f aith that he has a right to stop the path. Z is thereby prevented from passing. A wrongfully restrains Z.

340.title: Wrongful confinement
340.what: Wrongful confinement: Whoever wrongfully restrains any person in such a manner as to prevent that person from proceedings beyond certain circumscribing limits, is said “wrongfully to confine” that person. Illustrations (a) A causes Z to go within a walled space, and locks Z inZ is thus prevented from proceeding in any direction beyond the circumscribing line of wall. A wrongfully confines Z. (b) A p laces men with firearms at the outlets of a building, and tells Z that they will fire at Z if Z attempts leave the building. A wrongfully confines Z.

341.title: Puni shment for wrongful restraint
341.what: Punishment for wrongful restraint: Whoever wrongfully restrains any person shall be punished with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to one month, or with fine which may extend to five hundred rupees, or with both.

342.title: Punish ment for wrongful confinement
342.what: Punishment for wrongful confinement: Whoever wrongfully confines an y person shall be punished with imprisonment of either de scription for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both.

343.title: Wrongful confinement for three or more days
343.what: Wrongful confinement for three or more days: Whoever wrongfully confines any person for three days, or more, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.

344.title: Wrongful confinement for ten or more days
344.what: Wrongful confinement for ten or more days: Whoever wrongfully confines any person for ten days, or more, shall be punished with imprisonment of ei ther description for a term which may extend to three years, and shall also be liable to fine.

345.title: Wrongful confinement of person for whose liberation writ has been issued
345.what: Whoever keeps any person in wrongful confinement, knowing that a writ for the liberation of that person has been duly issued, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years in addition to any term of imprisonment to which he may be liable under any other section of this Chapter.

346.title: Wrongful confinement in secret
346.what: A person who secretly confines someone without letting anyone know, including public servants or the person's family, can get up to 2 years in prison and additional punishments.

347.title: Wrongful confinement to extort property , or constrain to illegal act
347.what: A person who wrongfully confines someone to get money or property, or forces them to do something illegal, can be imprisoned for up to 3 years and fined.

348.title: Wrongful confinement to extort confession, or c ompel restoration of property
348.what: A person who wrongly confines someone to get a confession or information, or to force them to return property, can be punished with up to 3 years in prison and a fine.

349.title: Force
349.what: A person uses force if they cause another person's motion, change in motion, or stop motion, or if they make a substance move, change its motion, or stop it so that it touches another person's body, something they are wearing, or something near them that affects their sense of touch. This can be done in three ways: by using their own body power, by making a substance move without doing anything else, or by making an animal move.

350.title: Criminal force
350.what: A person intentionally uses force against another person without their consent, with the intention of committing an offence or causing harm, fear, or annoyance to the other person.

351.title: Assault
351.what: Whoever makes any gesture, or any preparation intending or knowing it to be likely that such gesture or preparation will cause any person present to apprehend that he who makes that gesture or preparation is about to use criminal force to that person, is said to commit an assault.

352.title: Punishment for assault or criminal force otherw ise than on grave provocation
352.what: A person who assaults someone without serious reason will be punished with up to 3 months in prison, or a fine of up to 500 rupees, or both.

353.title: Assault or criminal force to deter public serva nt from discharge of his duty
353.what: A person who assaults or uses force to prevent a public servant from doing their job will be punished with imprisonment for up to 2 years, or a fine, or both.

354.title: Assault or criminal force to woman with intent to outrag e her modesty
354.what: A man who physically harms or uses force against a woman with the intention of humiliating her, can face imprisonment for at least one year and up to five years, and may also be fined.

354A.title: Sexual harassment and punishment for sexual harassment
354A.what: A person committing any of the following acts will be guilty of sexual harassment: physical contact and advances involving unwelcome and explicit sexual overtures, demanding or requesting sexual favors, showing pornography against a woman's will, or making sexually colored remarks. The punishment for this offense can be imprisonment for up to 3 years, fine, or both.

354B.title: Assault or use of criminal force to woman with intent to disrobe
354B.what: A man who assaults or uses force on a woman to disrobe her or compel her to be naked will face imprisonment of at least 3 years and up to 7 years, plus a fine.

354C.title: Voyeurism
354C.what: A man who watches a woman during a private moment without her consent and shares the image will get at least 1 year in prison and/or a fine. If he does it again, he'll get at least 3 years in prison and/or a fine.

354D.title: Stalking
354D.what: This section defines stalking and prescribes punishment for it.

354E.title: Liability person present who fails to prevent the commission of offence under Section 354,
354E.what: Whoever, being present at the time of commission of an offence under section 354, section 354A, section 354B, section 354C or section 354D and being able to prevent such offence, fails to prevent the commission of such offence or not being in position to prevent the commission of such offence, fails to give information of the commission of such offence to the nearest magistrate or police officer, by any mode, with the intention of screening the offender from legal punishment, shall be liable for abetment of such offence and shall be punished with imprisonment of either description which may extend to three years or with fine or with both.

355.title: Assault or criminal force with in tent to dishonour person, otherw ise than on grave
355.what: A person who assaults someone with the intention of dishonoring them, but not due to grave and sudden provocation, can face up to 2 years in prison, a fine, or both.

356.title: Assault or criminal force in attempt to commit theft of property carried by a person
356.what: A person who assaults or uses force to steal someone's property they are wearing or carrying will face up to 2 years in prison, or a fine, or both.

357.title: Assault or criminal force in attempt wrongfully to confine a person
357.what: A person who tries to wrongly confine someone by using force or threatening them will get up to 1 year in prison, or a fine of up to 1000 rupees, or both.

358.title: Assault or crimin al force on grave provocation
358.what: Assaulting someone on grave and sudden provocation can lead to a maximum of one month in prison, or a fine of up to 200 rupees, or both.

359.title: Kidnapping
359.what: Kidnapping is defined as taking a person away against their will, with two types: kidnapping from within India and kidnapping from lawful guardianship.

360.title: Kidnapping from India
360.what: Conveying a person beyond India's borders without their consent or authorized consent

361.title: Kidnapping from lawful guardianship
361.what: Whoever takes or entices any minor under 2[sixteen] years of age if a male, or under 3[eighteen] years of age if a female, or any person of unsound mind, out of the keeping of the lawful guardian of such minor or person of unsound mind, without the consent of such guardian, is said to kidnap such minor or person from lawful guardianship.

362.title: Abduction
362.what: A person is considered abducted if they are forced or deceived into leaving a place against their will.

363.title: Punishment for kidnapping
363.what: A person who takes someone without their consent from India or from a legal guardian will get up to 7 years in prison and have to pay a fine.

363A.title: Kidnapping or maiming a minor for purposes of begging
363A.what: Kidnapping or maiming a minor for purposes of begging is punishable with imprisonment of either description for up to 10 years and/or fine. Maiming a minor for this purpose can result in life imprisonment and/or fine.

364.title: Kidnapping or abducting in order to murder
364.what: A person who kidnaps or abducts someone with the intention of killing them, putting them in danger of being killed, or disposing of them to face harm, will be punished with imprisonment for life or up to 10 years and a fine.

364A.title: Kidnapping for ransom, etc
364A.what: Whoever kidnaps or abducts a person and threatens to cause harm or death, or gives reason to believe they may be harmed, in order to compel someone to do an act, pay a ransom, or abstain from doing something, shall face the death penalty, life imprisonment, or fine.

365.title: Kidnapping or abducting with intent secretly and wrongfully to confine person
365.what: A person who takes someone without their consent with the intention of keeping them hidden and against their will can face up to 7 years in prison and a fine.

366.title: Kidnapping, abducting or inducing woman to compel her marriage, etc
366.what: A person who kidnaps or abducts a woman with the intention of forcing her into marriage against her will, or knowing it is likely that she will be forced into marriage, can face up to 10 years in prison and a fine. Additionally, if they use intimidation, abuse of authority, or any other method to compel the woman to go somewhere with them, they can also face up to 10 years in prison and a fine.

366A.title: Procuration of minor girl
366A.what: Whoever, by any means whatsoever, induces any minor girl under the age of eighteen years to go from any place or to do any act with intent that such girl may be, or knowing that it is likely that she will be, for ced or seduced to illicit intercourse with another person shall be punishable with imprisonment which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.

366B.title: Importation of girl from foreign country
366B.what: A person who brings a girl under 21 from outside India (or Jammu and Kashmir) with the intention of forcing her into sex or knowing it's likely she will be, faces up to 10 years in prison and a fine.

367.title: Kidnapping or abducting in order to subject person to grievous hurt, slavery, etc
367.what: A person who kidnaps or abducts someone to put them in danger of being hurt severely, enslaved, or subjected to unnatural desires will face up to 10 years in prison and a fine.

368.title: Wrongfully concealing or keeping in confinement, kidnapped or abducted person
368.what: A person who knows someone has been kidnapped or abducted and then wrongfully hides or keeps them in captivity will be punished as if they had committed the kidnapping or abduction themselves.

369.title: Kidnapping or abducting child under ten years with in tent to steal from its person
369.what: A person who takes a child under 10 years old with the intention of stealing something from them can get up to 7 years in prison and a fine.

370.title: Trafficking of person
370.what: A person commits the offence of trafficking by recruiting, transporting, harbouring, transferring, or receiving a person using threats, force, coercion, abduction, fraud, deception, abuse of power, or inducement, with the consent of the person having control over the victim.

370A.title: Exploitation of a trafficked person
370A.what: Exploiting someone who has been trafficked for sexual exploitation is punishable by: - 5-7 years in prison - Fine

371.title: Habitual dealing in slaves
371.what: Habitually importing, exporting, removing, buying, selling, trafficking, or dealing in slaves. Punishment includes imprisonment for life or up to 10 years, and fine.

372.title: Selling minor for purposes of prostitution, etc
372.what: Selling minor for purposes of prostitution, etc - Whoever sells, lets to hire, or otherwise disposes of any person under the age of eighteen years with intent that such person shall at any age be employed or used for the purpose of prostitution or illicit intercourse with any person or for any unlawful and immoral purpose, or knowing it to be likely that such person will at any age be employed or used for any such purpose, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.

373.title: Buying minor for purposes of prostitution, etc
373.what: A person who buys, hires or obtains a minor (under 18 years old) with the intention of using them for prostitution or any other immoral purpose will be punished with up to 10 years in prison and a fine.

374.title: Unlawful compulsory labour
374.what: A person who forces someone to work without their consent can get up to 1 year in prison, or a fine, or both.

376.title: Punishment for rape
376.what: Section 376 states that whoever commits rape, except in the cases provided for in sub-section (2), shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment of either description for a term which shall not be less than ten years, but which may extend to imprisonment for life, and shall also be liable to fine.

376A.title: Punishment for causing death or resulting in persistent vegetative state of victim
376A.what: Whoever commits an offence punishable under sub-section (1) or sub-section (2) of section 376 and in the course of such commission inflicts an injury which causes the death of the woman or causes the woman to be in a persistent vegetative state, shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than twenty years, but which may extend to imprisonment for life, which shall mean imprisonment for the remainder of that person's natural life, or with death.

376B.title: Sexual intercourse by husband upon his wife during separation
376B.what: A man who has sex with his wife while she is separated from him without her consent must be imprisoned for at least 2 years and up to 7 years, and may also receive a fine.

376C.title: Sexual intercourse by a person in authority
376C.what: A person in a position of authority, fiduciary relationship, or public service who abuses their power to induce or seduce someone under their care into having sexual intercourse will be punished with at least 5 years and up to 10 years in prison and may also receive a fine.

376E.title: Punishment for repeat offenders
376E.what: Punishment for repeat offenders: Whoever has been previously convicted of an offence punishable under sections 376, 376A, or any of the specified sections and is subsequently convicted of an offence punishable under any of those sections shall be punished with imprisonment for life or death.

376F.title: Liability of person in-charge of workplace and others to give information about offence
376F.what: A person in charge of a workplace or anyone present at the place who knows an offence under sections 376 or 376D is being committed and has the power to prevent it but fails to do so, shall be punished with imprisonment up to 3 years and fine.

377.title: Unnatural offences
377.what: A person who engages in non-consensual sexual activity with another person or animal will face imprisonment for up to 10 years and/or a fine.

378.title: Theft
378.what: Section 378 states that whoever, intending to take dishonestly any movable property out of the possession of any person without that person's consent, moves that property in order to such taking, is said to commit theft.

379.title: Punishment for theft
379.what: A person who steals something can get up to 3 years in prison or a fine or both.

379A.title: Snatching
379A.what: Snatching: Whoever, with the intention to commit theft, suddenly or quickly or forcibly seizes or secures or grabs or takes away from any person or from his physical possession any movable property, and makes or attempts to make escape with such property, is said to commit snatching.

380.title: Theft in dwelling house, etc
380.what: A person who steals something from a building, tent, or boat that is used as a home or to store things can get up to 7 years in prison and have to pay a fine.

381.title: Theft by clerk or servant of property in possession of maste r
381.what: A person who is a clerk, servant, or employee commits theft if they take property that belongs to their employer while it is in the employer's possession.

382.title: Theft after preparation made for causing death, hurt or restraint in order to the committing
382.what: Whoever commits theft with preparation for causing death, hurt, or restraint shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment up to 10 years and fine.

382B.title: Whoever commits ‘Snatching’ shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which shall not
382B.what: A person who takes something away from someone by force or threat must face a prison sentence of at least 7 years, up to 10 years, or a fine (or both).

382C.title: Vehicle lifting: Whoever commits theft of a ‘vehicle’ either from open or close arena, is said to
382C.what: A person who steals a vehicle from an open or closed area is guilty of 'vehicle lifting'.

382D.title: Whoever commits the offence of ‘vehicle lifting’ shall be punished with imprisonment for a term
382D.what: A person who lifts a vehicle must face at least 7 years in prison, up to 10 years, or a fine (or both)

382E.title: Cattle lifting: Whoever commits theft of a ‘Cattle’ either from open or close arena, is said to
382E.what: Whoever commits theft of a 'Cattle' either from open or close arena is said to commit the offence of 'Cattle lifting'. A 'Cattle' means a cow and a calf, bull, bullock, buffalo-male or female, she-buffalo, ox or oxen.

382F.title: Whoever commits the offence of ‘Cattle lifting’ shall be punished with imprisonment for a term
382F.what: Whoever commits the offence of 'Cattle lifting' shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than seven years but may extend to a term of ten years or with fine or with both.

383.title: Extortion
383.what: A person commits extortion by intentionally putting someone in fear of harm or injury to themselves or others, with the goal of getting them to give something of value, such as money, property, or a signed document.

384.title: Punishment for extortion
384.what: A person who commits extortion can be punished with up to 3 years in prison, a fine, or both.

385.title: Putting person in fear of injury in order to commit extortion
385.what: Punishment for putting someone in fear to commit extortion

386.title: Extortion by putting a person in fear of death or grievous hurt
386.what: A person who threatens someone with death or serious injury to get something from them will face up to 10 years in prison and a fine.

387.title: Putting person in fear of death or of grievous hurt, in order to commit extortion
387.what: A person who tries to scare someone into giving money or something else will get up to 7 years in jail and possibly a fine.

388.title: Extortion by threat of accusation of an offence punishable with death or imprisonment for
388.what: A person who threatens someone with an accusation of a serious crime (like death or long imprisonment) can be punished with up to 10 years in prison and/or fined.

389.title: Putting person in fear or accusation of offence, in order to commit extortion
389.what: Whoever, in order to the committing of extortion, puts or attempts to put any person in fear of an accusation, against that person or any other, of having committed, or attempted to commit, an offence punishable with death or with imprisonment for life, or with imprisonment for a term which may extend to ten years, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine; and, if the offence be punishable under section 377 of this Code, may be punished with imprisonment for life.

390.title: Robbery
390.what: Section 390 states that robbery is defined as theft where the offender causes or attempts to cause death or hurt or wrongful restraint to any person, or puts a person in fear of instant death or of instant hurt or of instant wrongful restraint.

391.title: Dacoity
391.what: Section 391 defines dacoity as when five or more persons conjointly commit or attempt to commit a robbery, and every person committing, attempting, or aiding such commission or attempt is said to commit dacoity.

392.title: Punishment for robbery
392.what: Section 392 states that whoever commits robbery shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine; and if the robbery be committed on the highway between sunset and sunrise, the imprisonment may be extended to fourteen years.

393.title: Attemp t to commit robbery
393.what: Section 393 states that whoever attempts to commit robbery shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.

394.title: Voluntarily causi ng hurt in committing robbery
394.what: Section 394 states that if any person, in committing or attempting to commit robbery, voluntarily causes hurt, such person and any other person jointly concerned in committing or attempting to commit such robbery shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or with rigorous imprisonment for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.

395.title: Punishment for dacoity
395.what: Section 395 states that whoever commits dacoity shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or with rigorous imprisonment for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.

396.title: Dacoity with mu rder
396.what: Section 396 states that if any one of five or more persons who are conjointly committing dacoity commits murder in so committing dacoity, every one of those persons shall be punished with death, or imprisonment for life, or rigorous imprisonment for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.

397.title: Robbery , or dacoity, with attempt to cause death or grievous hurt
397.what: Section 397 states that if at the time of committing robbery or dacoity, the offender uses any deadly weapon, or causes grievous hurt to any person, or attempts to cause death or grievous hurt to any person, the imprisonment with which such offender shall be punished shall not be less than seven years.

398.title: Attempt to commit robbery or dacoity when armed with deadly weapon
398.what: If, at the time of attempting to commit robbery or dacoity, the offender is armed with any deadly weapon, the imprisonment with which such offender shall be punished shall not be less than seven years.

399.title: Making preparation to commit dacoity
399.what: Whoever makes any preparation for committing dacoity, shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.

400.title: Punishment for belonging to gang of dacoits
400.what: Whoever, at any time after the passing of this Act, shall belong to a gang of persons associated for the purpose of habitually committing dacoity, shall be punished with 1[imprisonment for life], or with rigorous imprisonment for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.

401.title: Punishment for belonging to gang of thieves
401.what: Whoever, at any time after the passing of this Act, shall belong to any wandering or other gang of persons associated for the purpose of habitually committing theft or robbery, and not being a gang of thugs or dacoits, shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.

402.title: Assembling for purpose of committing dacoity
402.what: Whoever, at any time after the passing of this Act, shall be one of five or more persons assembled for the purpose of committing dacoity, shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.

403.title: Dishonest misappropriation of property
403.what: Whoever dishonestly misappropriates or converts to his own use any movable property, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.

404.title: Dishonest misappropriation of property possessed by deceased p erson at the time of his
404.what: Whoever dishonestly misappropriates or converts t o his own use property, knowing that such property was in the possession of a deceased person at the time of that person's decease, and has not since been in the possession of any person legally entitled to such possession, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, and shall also be liable to fine,

405.title: Criminal breach of trust
405.what: Section 405 states that whoever, being in any manner entrusted with property, or with any dominion over property, dishonestly misappropriates or converts to his own use that property, or dishonestly uses or disposes of that property in violation of any direction of law prescribing the mode in which such trust is to be discharged, or of any legal contract, express or implied, which he has made touching the discharge of such trust, or wilfully suffers any other person so to do, commits criminal breach of trust.

406.title: Punishment for criminal breach of trust
406.what: A person who breaks the trust of another can be punished with up to 3 years in prison, or a fine, or both.

407.title: Criminal breach of trust by carrier, etc
407.what: A person who is entrusted with someone else's property (like a carrier, wharfinger or warehouse-keeper) commits a crime if they misuse that property.

408.title: Criminal breach of trust by clerk or servant
408.what: A person who is a clerk or servant and has control over property must return it according to the rules and face penalties, including up to 7 years in prison and fines.

409.title: Criminal breach of trust by public servant, or by banker, merchant or agent
409.what: A public servant or someone in business as a banker, merchant, factor, broker, attorney or agent who misuses property they were entrusted with will get up to 10 years in prison and/or be fined.

410.title: Stolen property
410.what: Stolen property refers to property that was obtained through theft, extortion, robbery, or criminal misappropriation. This includes property that has been transferred without permission and property where a breach of trust has occurred. Stolen property can still be considered stolen if it is later found by someone who does not have the right to possess it.

411.title: Dishones tly receiving stolen property
411.what: A person who knowingly receives or keeps stolen property will face punishment, including up to 3 years in prison, a fine, or both.

412.title: Dishonestly receiving property stolen in the commission of a dacoity
412.what: Dishonestly receiving property stolen in the commission of a dacoity: Whoever dishonestly receives or retains any stolen property, the possession whereof he knows or has reason to believe to have been transferred by the commission of dacoity, or dishonestly receives from a person, whom he knows or has reason to believe to belong or to have belonged to a gang of dacoits, property which he knows or has reason to believe to be stolen, shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or with rigorous imprisonment for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.

413.title: Habitually dealing in stolen property
413.what: Habitually dealing in stolen property: Whoever habitually receives or deals in property which he knows or has reason to believe to be stolen property, shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.

414.title: Assisting in c oncealment of stolen property
414.what: Assisting in concealment of stolen property: Whoever voluntarily assists in concealing or disposing of or making away with property which he knows or has reason to believe to be stolen property, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both.

415.title: Cheating
415.what: Cheating: Whoever, by deceiving any person, fraudulently or dishonestly induces the person so deceived to deliver any property to any person, or to consent that any person shall retain any property, or intentionally induces the person so deceived to do or omit to do anything which he would not do or omit if he were not so deceived, and which act or omission causes or is likely to cause damage or harm to that person in body, mind, reputation or property, is said to “cheat”.

416.title: Cheating by personation
416.what: Cheating by personation: A person is said to “cheat by personation” if he cheats by pretending to be some other person, or by knowingly substituting one person for or another, or representing that he or any other person is a person other than he or such other person really is.

417.title: Punishment for cheating
417.what: Punishment for cheating: Whoever cheats shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine, or with both.

418.title: Cheating with knowledge that wrongful loss may ensue to person whose interest offender is
418.what: Cheating with knowledge that wrongful loss may ensue to person whose interest offender is bound to protect.—Whoever cheats with the knowledge that he is likely thereby to cause wrongful loss to a person whose interest in the transaction to which the cheating relates, he was bound, either by law, or by a legal contract, to protect, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both.

419.title: Punishment for cheating by personation
419.what: Punishment for cheating by personation: Whoever cheats by personation shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both.

420.title: Cheating and dishonestly i nducing delivery of property
420.what: Section 420 states that whoever cheats and dishonestly induces the person deceived to deliver any property to any person, or to make, alter or destroy the whole or any part of a valuable security, or anything which is signed or sealed, and which is capable of being converted into a valuable security, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.

421.title: Dishonest or fraudulent removal or concealment of property to prevent distribution among
421.what: Section 421 states that whoever dishonestly or fraudulently removes, conceals or delivers to any person, or transfers or causes to be transferred to any person, without adequate consideration, any property, intending thereby to prevent, or knowing it to be likely that he will thereby prevent, the distribution of that property according to law among his creditors or the creditors of any other person, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.

422.title: Dishonestly or fraudulent ly preventing debt being available for creditors
422.what: Section 422 states that whoever dishonestly or fraudulently prevents any debt or demand due to himself or to any other person from being made available according to law for payment of his debts or the debts of such other person, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.

423.title: Dishonest or fraudulent execution of deed of transfer containing fal se statement of
423.what: Section 423 states that whoever dishonestly or fraudulently signs, executes or becomes a party to any deed or instrument which purports to transfer or subject to any charge any property, or any interest therein, and which contains any false statement relating to the consideration for such transfer or charge, or relating to the person or persons for whose use or benefit it is really intended to operate, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.

424.title: Dishonest or fraudulen t remov al or concealment of property
424.what: Section 424 states that whoever dishonestly or fraudulently conceals or removes any property of himself or any other person, or dishonestly or fraudulently assists in the concealment or removal thereof, or dishonestly releases any demand or claim to which he is entitled, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.

425.title: Mischief
425.what: Section 425 states that whoever with intent to cause, or knowing that he is likely to cause, wrongful loss or damage to the public or to any person, causes the destruction of any property, or any such change in any property or in the situation thereof as destroys or diminishes its value or utility, or affects it injuriously, commits mischief.

426.title: Punishment for mischief
426.what: Section 426 states that whoever commits mischief shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three months, or with fine, or with both.

427.title: Mischief causing damage t o the amount of fifty rupees
427.what: Section 427 states that whoever commits mischief and thereby causes loss or damage to the amount of fifty rupees or upwards, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.

428.title: Mischief by killing or maiming animal of the value of ten rupees
428.what: Whoever commits mischief by killing, poisoning, maiming or rendering useless any animal or animals of the value of the ten rupees or upwards, shall be punished with imprisonment of either descripti on for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.

429.title: Mischief by killing or maiming cattle, etc., of any value or any animal of the value of fifty
429.what: Whoever commits mischief by killing, poisoning, maiming or rendering useless any animal worth 50 rupees or more will face up to 5-year imprisonment, or a fine, or both.

430.title: Mischief by injury to works of irrigation or by wro ngfully diverting water
430.what: Whoever commits mischief by doing any act which causes, or which he knows to be likely to cause, a diminution of the supply of water for agricultural purposes, or for food or drink for human beings or for animals which are property, or for cleanliness or for carrying on any manufacture, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to five years, or with fine, or with both.

431.title: Mischief by injury to public r oad, bridge, river or channel
431.what: Whoever commits mischief by doing any act which renders or which he knows to be likely to render any public road, bridge, navigable river or navigable channel, natural or artificial, impassable or less safe for travelling or conveying property.

432.title: Mischief by causing inundation or obstruction to public drainage attended with damage
432.what: Causing mischief that causes flooding or blockage of public drains and results in damage.

433.title: Mischief by destroying, moving or rendering less use ful a light -house or sea -mark
433.what: Whoever commits mischief by destroying or moving any light-house or sea-mark, or any sea-mark or buoy or other thing placed as a guide for navigators, or by any act which renders any such light-house, sea-mark, buoy or other such thing as aforesaid less useful as a guide for navigators, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, or with fine, or with both.

434.title: Mischief by destroying or moving, etc., a land -mark fixed by public authority
434.what: Whoever commits mischief by destroying or moving any landmark fixed by the authority of a public servant, or by any act which renders such landmark less useful as such, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine, or with both.

435.title: Mischief by fire or explosive substance with intent to cause damage to amount of one
435.what: Whoever commits mischief by fire or any explosive substance intending to cause damage to any property worth one hundred rupees or more (or ten rupees or more if the property is agricultural produce) will face up to 7 years in prison and a fine.

436.title: Mischief by fire or explosive substance with intent to destroy house, etc
436.what: Whoever commits mischief by fire or any explosive substance, intending to cause, or knowing it to be likely that he will thereby cause, the destruction of any building which is ordinarily used as a place of worship or as a human dwelling or as a place for the custody of property, shall be punished with 2[imprisonment for life], or with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.

437.title: Mischief with intent to destroy or make unsafe a decked vessel or one of twenty tons
437.what: A person who intentionally damages or makes a ship unsafe (if the ship is 20 tons or more) can get up to 10 years in prison and a fine.

438.title: Punis hment for the mischief described in section 437 committed by fire or explosive
438.what: Punishment: Up to imprisonment for life or up to 10 years and fine

439.title: Punishment for intentionally running vessel aground or ashore with intent to commit theft,
439.what: A person who intentionally runs a vessel aground or ashore to commit theft or dishonestly take property will face up to 10 years in prison and a fine.

440.title: Mischief committed after preparation made for causing death or hurt
440.what: A person who causes damage after preparing to harm someone's life, health, freedom, or safety will face up to 5 years in prison and a possible fine.

441.title: Criminal trespass
441.what: A person who enters or remains on someone else's property with the intention of committing a crime, intimidating, insulting, or annoying the owner, is guilty of

442.title: House -trespass
442.what: A person who enters or stays in a building used for human dwelling, worship, or property custody without permission commits 'house-trespass'.

444.title: Lurking house-trespass by night
444.what: Section 444 states that lurking house-trespass by night refers to committing house-trespass after sunset and before sunrise.

446.title: House-breaking by night
446.what: A person who breaks into a house between sunset and sunrise is guilty of 'house-breaking by night'.

447.title: Punishment for criminal trespass
447.what: A person who enters someone else's property without permission can be punished with up to 3 months in jail, a fine of up to ₹500, or both.

448.title: Punishment for house -trespass
448.what: A person who enters someone else's house without permission can be punished with up to 1 year in prison, or fined up to ₹1000, or both.

449.title: House-trespass in order to commit offence punishable with death
449.what: A person who breaks into someone's house to commit a crime that can result in the death of the victim will be punished with either life imprisonment or up to 10 years in prison and may also have to pay a fine.

450.title: House-trespass in order to commit offence punishable with imprisonment for life
450.what: A person who breaks into someone's house to commit an offense that can lead to a life sentence will get up to 10 years in prison and may have to pay a fine.

451.title: House -trespass in order to commit offence punishable with imprisonment
451.what: A person who breaks into someone's house with the intention of committing a crime that can result in jail time will get up to 2 years in prison and/or a fine. If they're trying to steal, they could get up to 7 years in prison.

452.title: House-trespass alter preparation for hurt, assault or wrongful restraint
452.what: Whoever commits house-trespass, having made preparation for causing hurt to any person or for assaulting any person, or for wrongfully restraining any person, or for putting a person in fear of hurt, or of assault , or of wrongful restraint, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.

453.title: Punishment for lurking house-trespass or house-breaking
453.what: A person who breaks into a house without being invited can get up to 2 years in prison and/or be fined.

454.title: Lurking house -trespass or house -breaking in order to commit offence punishable with
454.what: A person who breaks into a house with the intention of committing an offense that can result in imprisonment will receive up to 3 years in prison and/or a fine. If the intended crime is theft, the sentence can be up to 10 years.

455.title: Lurking house-trespass or house-breaking after preparation for hurt, assault or wrongful
455.what: Whoever commits lurking house-trespass, or house-breaking, having made preparation for causing hurt to any person, or for assaulting any person, or for wrongfully restraining any person, or for putting any person in fear of hurt or of assault or of wrongful restraint, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description or a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.

456.title: Punishment for lurking house -trespass or house -breaking by night
456.what: A person who breaks into a house at night without permission will be imprisoned for up to 3 years and fined.

457.title: Lurking house-trespass or house-breaking by night in order to commit offence punishable
457.what: Whoever commits lurking house-trespass by night, or house-breaking by night, in order to commit an offence punishable with imprisonment, shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to five years and shall also be liable to fine. If the offence intended is theft, the term of imprisonment may be extended to fourteen years.

458.title: Lurking house-trespass or house-breaking by night after preparation for hurt, a ssault, or
458.what: Whoever commits lurking house-trespass by night, or house-breaking by night, having made preparation for causing hurt to any person or for assaulting any person, or for wrongfully restraining any person, or for putting any person in fear of hurt, or of assault, or of wrongful restraint, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to fourteen years, and shall also be liable to fine.

459.title: Grievous hurt caused whilst committing lurking hous e-trespass o r house -breaking
459.what: Causing grievous hurt while committing house-trespass or house-breaking, or attempting to cause death or grievous hurt.

460.title: All persons jointly concerned in lurking house -trespass or house -breaking by night
460.what: Punishable where death or grievous hurt caused by one of them.—If, at the time of the committing of lurking house-trespass by night or house-breaking by night, any person guilty of such offence shall voluntarily cause or attempt to cause death or grievous hurt to any person, every person jointly concerned in committing such lurkking house-trespass by night or house-breaking by night, shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.

461.title: Dishonestly breaking open recep tacle containing property
461.what: A person who intentionally opens a container that might have something valuable inside will get up to 2 years in jail, or a fine, or both.

462.title: Punishment for same offence when committed by person entrusted with custody
462.what: A person who breaks open a closed receptacle containing property without permission will be punished with imprisonment for up to 3 years, or a fine, or both.

463.title: Forgery
463.what: A person who creates a false document or electronic record with the intention of causing harm or injury to someone or something, or to gain an advantage through deception, commits forgery.

464.title: Making a false document
464.what: Section 464 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 states that whoever makes or alters any document or electronic record with the intention of deceiving others into believing it was created or altered by someone else without their actual authority, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years and shall also be liable to fine. Additionally, making a false document in the name of a fictitious person or a deceased person with intent to deceive is considered forgery, punishable under this section.

465.title: Punishment for forgery
465.what: Whoever commits forgery shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.

466.title: Forgery of record of Court or of public register, etc
466.what: Forging a document or electronic record that appears to be from a court, public register, or official document can lead to up to 7 years in prison and a fine.

467.title: Forgery of valuable security, will, etc
467.what: Forging a document that appears to be a valuable security, will, or authority, with penalties including imprisonment for life and fine.

468.title: Forgery for purpose of cheating
468.what: A person who creates a fake document or record with the intention of deceiving others will face up to 7 years in prison and a fine.

469.title: Forgery for purpose of harming reputation
469.what: A person who commits forgery intending to harm someone's reputation can get up to 3 years in prison and a fine.

470.title: Forged document
470.what: A false document or electronic record made wholly or in part by forgery is called a forged document.

471.title: Using as genuine a forged document or electronic record
471.what: Using a forged document or electronic record with the intention of deceiving others, knowing it is fake, and facing punishment for forging it.

472.title: Making or possessing counterfeit seal, etc., with intent to commit forgery punishable under section
472.what: Making or possessing counterfeit seal, etc., with intent to commit forgery punishable under section 467.

473.title: Making or possessing counterfeit seal, etc., with intent to commi t forgery punishable otherwise
473.what: Making or possessing counterfeit seal, etc., with intent to commit forgery punishable otherwise

474.title: Having possession of document described in section 466 or 467, knowing it to be forged and
474.what: Possessing a forged document with the intention of using it as genuine. If the document is one of two types (described in sections 466 or 467), punishment includes imprisonment for up to 7 years and/or fine. For the other type, punishment includes imprisonment for life and/or up to 7 years and/or fine.

475.title: Counterfeiting device or mark used for authenticating documents described in section 467,
475.what: Counterfeiting device or mark used for authenticating documents described in section 467, or possessing counterfeit marked material. Anyone who counterfeits or possesses such material with the intention of giving it a false appearance of authenticity will face imprisonment for life or up to seven years and a fine.

476.title: Counterfeiting device or mark used for authenticating documents other than those described
476.what: Counterfeiting device or mark used for authenticating documents other than those described, with intent to give appearance of authenticity to any document then forged or thereafter to be forged on such material.

477.title: Fraudulent cancellation, destruction, etc., of will, authority to adopt, or valuable security
477.what: A person who intentionally destroys, alters, or conceals a will, adoption authority, or valuable security document with the goal of causing harm to someone or the public can face up to 7 years in prison and/or a fine.

479.title: Property mark
479.what: A mark used to show that movable property belongs to a particular person is called a property mark.

482.title: Punishment for using a false property mark
482.what: A person who uses a false property mark (except if they can prove it was not done with the intention to deceive) will face punishment. The punishment can be imprisonment for up to 1 year, a fine, or both.

483.title: Counterfeiting a property mark used by another
483.what: Counterfeiting a property mark used by another can result in imprisonment for up to 2 years, or a fine, or both.

484.title: Counterfeiting a mark used by a public servant
484.what: Counterfeiting a mark used by a public servant, using it as genuine knowing it to be counterfeit, can lead to imprisonment of up to three years and fine.

485.title: Making or possession of any instrument for c ounterfeiting a property mark
485.what: Making or possessing an instrument to counterfeit a property mark can result in up to 3 years of imprisonment, a fine, or both.

486.title: Selling goods marked with a counterfeit property mark
486.what: Selling goods marked with a counterfeit property mark. If you sell goods with a fake mark, you can be punished with up to 1 year in prison, a fine, or both.

487.title: Making a false mark upon any receptacle containing goods
487.what: Making false marks on goods containers can lead to up to 3 years in prison, or a fine, or both.

488.title: Punishment for maki ng use of any such false mark
488.what: If you make use of a false mark, you will be punished like for committing an offence under this section, unless you can prove you didn't intend to deceive.

489.title: Tampering with property mark with intent to cause injury
489.what: Tampering with property mark with intent to cause injury

489A.title: Counterfeiting currency-notes or bank-notes
489A.what: Counterfeiting currency-notes or bank-notes: Whoever counterfeits or knowingly performs part of the process of counterfeiting currency-notes or bank-notes shall face imprisonment up to 10 years and/or fine.

489B.title: Using as genuine, forged or counterfeit currency-notes or bank-notes
489B.what: Selling, buying, or receiving forged or counterfeit currency-notes or bank-notes with knowledge of their forgery.

489C.title: Possession of forged or coun terfeit currency -notes or bank -notes
489C.what: Possession of forged or counterfeit currency-note or bank-note. If you have forged or counterfeit currency-note or bank-note in your possession and know it's fake, but plan to use it as if it's real, you can face up to 7 years in prison, a fine, or both.

489D.title: Making or possessing instruments or materials for forging or counterfeiting currency notes
489D.what: Making or possessing instruments or materials for forging or counterfeiting currency notes is punishable by up to 10 years in prison and/or a fine.

489E.title: Making or using documents resembling currency-notes or bank -notes
489E.what: Making or using documents resembling currency-notes or bank-notes: Anyone who creates, uses, or gives such documents to someone else can be fined up to ₹100. If the person whose name is on the document refuses to reveal their maker's identity without a valid reason, they can be fined up to ₹200.

491.title: Breach of contract to attend on and supply wants of helpless person
491.what: A person who has a contract to care for someone who is unable to take care of themselves due to youth, illness, or weakness, willfully fails to do so, may face imprisonment for up to 3 months, a fine of up to 200 rupees, or both.

493.title: Cohabitation caused by a man deceitfully inducing a belief of lawful marriage
493.what: A man who deceives a woman into believing she is married to him and they cohabitate or have sex will face up to 10 years in prison and a fine.

494.title: Marrying again durin g lifetime of husband or wife
494.what: Marrying again during lifetime of husband or wife: Punishment and exceptions

495.title: Same offence with concealment of former marriage from person with whom subs equent
495.what: Whoever commits the offence defined in the last preceding section having concealed from the person with whom the subsequent marriage is contracted, the fact of the former marriage, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.

496.title: Marriage ceremony fraudule ntly gone th rough without lawful marriage
496.what: A person who gets married fraudulently without having a lawful marriage can be imprisoned for up to 7 years and fined.

497.title: Adultery
497.what: A person who has sex with someone they know is married to, without their husband's consent, can get up to 5 years in jail or a fine.

498.title: Enticing or taking away or detaining with criminal intent a married woman
498.what: A man can be punished if he takes or entices away a married woman from her husband or someone looking after her, with the intention of having an illicit relationship with her.

498A.title: Husband or relative of husband of a woman subjecting her to cruelty
498A.what: The husband or relative of the husband of a woman who subjects her to cruelty can be punished with up to 3 years imprisonment and fined.

499.title: Defamation
499.what: Section 499 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 states that whoever publishes or circulates any statement, rumour, charge or slanderous matter with the intent to lower the estimation of a public servant, public figure or institution, shall be punished. However, it is not defamation to make an imputation on the character of another if made in good faith for the protection of one's own interests, for the public good, or for the good of a person to whom it is conveyed.

500.title: Punishment for defamation
